39828227.conclusion_quote: C16 plus Ang-1 might serve as a complement to GCs for the treatment of MS.
39828227.summary: In rats with acute experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, C16 peptide with angiopoietin-1 protected nerves and caused fewer steroid side effects than high-dose methylprednisolone.

40152123.mechanism: Reduces STAT1, raising IFI30 to limit oxidative damage
40152123.conclusion_quote: STAT1 silencing exhibits neuroprotective effects against ON by upregulating IFI30.
40152123.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of optic neuritis, knocking down the STAT1 gene reduced optic nerve inflammation, nerve damage, and retinal cell death.

38944109.conclusion_quote: We, therefore, provide here for the first time a detailed molecular description of specific HERV-W ENV evoked effects on those glial cell populations that are involved in smoldering neuroinflammatory processes relevant for progression of neurodegenerative diseases.
38944109.summary: This study compared gene activity in microglia and astroglia cells exposed to the HERV-W envelope protein with cells exposed to LPS, a bacterial inflammatory trigger, revealing distinct inflammatory changes.

39725338.mechanism: S1P receptor agonist reducing astrocyte activation and neuroinflammation
39725338.conclusion_quote: Our study underscores the beneficial therapeutic effects of FTY on HD involving endogenous steroid hormones and their important anabolic effects.
39725338.summary: In zQ175 mice modeling Huntington's disease, the MS drug fingolimod improved body weight and motor function, with stronger benefits in females than males.

40019134.conclusion_quote: Our study emphasises the need to balance field-of-view and voxel size when characterising white matter features across length scales.
40019134.summary: Using MRI and X-ray imaging in monkey and mouse brains, including mice given the toxin cuprizone to damage myelin, researchers found shared patterns in how nerve fibre bundles are arranged.

40476381.conclusion_quote: [ 18 F] 7a also showed good brain uptake and retention in macaque, and no radiometabolites entered the rat brain, further supporting its potential as a promising radiotracer for imaging S1PR5 in the brain.
40476381.summary: Researchers developed radiotracers to image the S1PR5 receptor in the brain, and one candidate showed good uptake in rats and macaques and reduced signal in mice fed cuprizone, a demyelination model.

40523590.mechanism: Not a treatment: chemical exposure only
40523590.conclusion_quote: Overall, this study offers an understanding of the developmental neurotoxicity of DEHP and its behavioral and demyelinating effects in zebrafish larvae during early developmental stages.
40523590.summary: In zebrafish larvae exposed to the plastic chemical DEHP, the chemical increased oxidative stress, lowered hormone levels, and reduced myelin-related genes and proteins, showing developmental nerve toxicity.

39323335.mechanism: Predicted to block Kv1.2 and Kv1.3 potassium channels
39323335.conclusion_quote: Three non-toxic KTxs, Leptukalin 3, 5, and 7, were successfully discovered from the cDNA library of H. lepturus venom gland.
39323335.summary: This computer-based study identified three scorpion venom peptides predicted to block potassium channels linked to autoimmune diseases including multiple sclerosis. No animals or patient cells were tested.

40495390.mechanism: Herbal extracts in nanoliposomes promote remyelination and neuroprotection
40495390.conclusion_quote: The GNLP in high doses had significant improvement compared to others, highlighting its potential as a promising therapy for demyelinating neuropathies, paving the way for advancements in neurobiomedical science.
40495390.summary: In cuprizone-treated mice with demyelination, high-dose nanoliposomes of Ginkgo biloba leaf extract improved outcomes more than the other treatments tested.

40221393.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that type I collagen secreted by monocyte-derived macrophages inhibited white matter regeneration, and therefore, the modulation of type I collagen metabolism might be a novel therapeutic target for white matter injury.
40221393.summary: In mice with lysolecithin-induced demyelination and stroke-like injury, type I collagen from macrophages blocked oligodendrocyte maturation and remyelination, slowing recovery of white matter.

40485011.mechanism: Inhibits HDAC3, restoring PDK4 iron homeostasis and reducing ferroptosis
40485011.conclusion_quote: HDAC3 drives ferroptosis in WMI via iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation, highlighting the HDAC3-PDK4 axis as a therapeutic target.
40485011.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, blocking the enzyme HDAC3 with RGFP966 reduced iron buildup and cell damage, preserving myelin and improving movement and memory.

39568369.mechanism: Inhibits SUMO E1 enzyme, lowering global SUMOylation levels
39568369.conclusion_quote: Our findings contribute to a better understanding of MS pathology, reveal the important role of SUMOylation in disease progression, and demonstrate the potential of the SUMO E1 inhibitor as a novel treatment for MS.
39568369.summary: In mice with EAE, the SUMO E1 inhibitor TAK-981 lowered brain SUMOylation and eased symptoms, while proteomic profiling revealed changes in inflammation and nerve-related proteins.

39767677.mechanism: Describes disease markers only, no treatment tested
39767677.conclusion_quote: The expression of p-tau increased with the progression of EAE, reaching the maximum in the chronic phase.
39767677.summary: Researchers measured amyloid and tau proteins in the spinal cord of mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, at different disease stages.

39060233.mechanism: Activates APJ receptor, limiting immune cell trafficking through lung
39060233.conclusion_quote: Here, we show that treatment with apelin, a secreted peptide ligand for the G protein-coupled receptor APJ/Aplnr, is protective in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), an animal model of MS.
39060233.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, treatment with the peptide apelin reduced immune cell entry into the brain and delayed and eased the disease.

39802871.mechanism: inhibits lymphocyte migration across blood vessel walls
39802871.conclusion_quote: PEPITEM has potent prophylactic potential against MS, providing a robust foundation for further exploration.
39802871.summary: In mice with EAE, daily PEPITEM peptide injections delayed disease onset, lessened severity, and reduced immune cell infiltration in the spinal cord.

39030955.mechanism: Boosts anti-inflammatory cytokines, reduces inflammatory cytokines
39030955.conclusion_quote: The administration of MSCs significantly improved clinical symptoms, attenuated inflammation, and reduced spinal cord demyelination in EAE, suggesting a potential protective effect on disease progression.
39030955.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, mesenchymal stem cell treatment eased symptoms, reduced spinal cord inflammation and demyelination, and boosted anti-inflammatory signals.

39069688.mechanism: Supports mitochondrial energy and reduces oxidative stress
39069688.conclusion_quote: The combination of Coenzyme Q10 and L-Carnitine has a synergistic effect in controlling gliosis in a rat model of MS, but synergism could not be demonstrated on anhedonia.
39069688.summary: In rats with cuprizone-induced MS, combining Coenzyme Q10 and L-Carnitine reduced brain gliosis and increased oligodendrocytes, but did not improve anhedonia.

38411708.mechanism: Restores TGF-β signalling, limits effector T cell activation
38411708.conclusion_quote: The above results suggested that the upregulation of TGF-β signal transduction may provide new ideas for the study of MS pathogenesis and have positive implications for the development of drugs for the treatment of autoimmune diseases.
38411708.summary: In mice with EAE, the artemisinin derivative TPN10475 calmed harmful T cell activation and inflammation, reducing disease by supporting TGF-β signalling.

38387051.mechanism: blocks lymphocyte homing glycan ligand to lymph nodes
38387051.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these results suggest that 6-sulfo sLeX glycan would serve as a novel target for MS.
38387051.summary: In mice with EAE, an antibody called SF1 that targets 6-sulfo sLeX sugar chains on lymph node blood vessels reduced symptoms and harmful T cells.

39481766.mechanism: activates mitochondrial enzyme that detoxifies reactive aldehydes
39481766.conclusion_quote: This indicates that ALDH2 could serve as a molecular target for MS control, with ALDH2 activators, like Alda-1 as potential neuroprotective candidates.
39481766.summary: Mice with a human-like ALDH2 deficiency had worse EAE motor problems and pain. The ALDH2 activator Alda-1 reduced pain and motor impairment in EAE mice.

37875228.mechanism: activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway, reducing oxidative stress
37875228.conclusion_quote: DHA could exert a beneficial effect on the clinic of MS, through the activation of the antioxidant factor Nrf2.
37875228.summary: In rats with EAE, an animal model of MS, regular injections of docosahexaenoic acid reduced oxidative stress and improved clinical disease scores.

39340612.mechanism: Treadmill running increases myelin protein and reduces demyelination
39340612.conclusion_quote: The exercise showed neuroprotective effects, as evidenced by decreased areas of demyelination and improved MBP expression.
39340612.summary: In rats given the cuprizone MS model, treadmill exercise before or during demyelination reduced myelin loss in the corpus callosum and raised myelin protein levels.

39068656.mechanism: delivers large molecules past blood brain barrier
39068656.conclusion_quote: The insights into treatment efficacy that can be provided by this protocol make it an important tool for CNS research.
39068656.summary: This protocol describes how to deliver proteins, peptides, and shRNAs directly into the spinal fluid of mice with EAE, a model of MS, past the blood brain barrier.

39596104.mechanism: Blocks TLR2/MyD88/IRF5 pathway, reducing M1 microglia activation
39596104.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our findings reveal that panobinostat significantly ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in mice by inhibiting oxidative stress-linked neuroinflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction.
39596104.summary: Mice with EAE, a model of MS, improved when given the drug panobinostat, with less nerve damage, reduced inflammation, and better mitochondrial function.

38395110.mechanism: reduces oxidative stress and inflammation, restores hippocampal signaling
38395110.conclusion_quote: The EtB induced learning and memory impairment; however, NEP dose-dependently restored these impairments to normal levels.
38395110.summary: In rats with ethidium bromide induced hippocampal demyelination, higher doses of injected norepinephrine reduced oxidative stress and inflammation and restored memory.

38485508.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these results suggest that autoimmune neuroinflammation alters structural plasticity in the hippocampus, possibly through the ERK-ARC pathway, indicating that this alteration may be associated with hippocampal dysfunctions in EAE.
38485508.summary: In mice with EAE, an animal model of MS, inflammation was found to weaken connections between hippocampal brain cells, possibly affecting behavior.

38612856.mechanism: Antioxidant and anti-apoptotic effects protect retinal ganglion cells
38612856.conclusion_quote: The intranasal administration of RNs is able to reduce RGC loss independent of the inflammatory and demyelinating effects on the optic nerve and the spinal cord.
38612856.summary: In mice with EAE, intranasal resveratrol nanoparticles given at half the previous oral dose significantly protected retinal ganglion cells from loss.

38335658.conclusion_quote: These results demonstrate the establishment of an in vitro model that can be used to mimic MOG-reactive T cell stimulation in vivo.
38335658.summary: Mouse immune cells stimulated with a myelin peptide in a dish showed that cannabidiol and THC reduced inflammatory signals, supporting a lab model of multiple sclerosis T cell activation.

38232534.mechanism: Blocks receptors, favoring non-canonical Notch-1 signaling
38232534.conclusion_quote: These results outlined the remyelinating beneficence of CLM which could be due to augmenting the non-canonical Notch-1 signaling over the canonical one.
38232534.summary: In rats with an MS-like disease called EAE, clemastine improved movement, mood and myelin repair, shifting Notch signaling toward the non-canonical pathway.

39228110.mechanism: Loss of astrocyte iron storage lowers oxidative stress
39228110.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these findings suggest that iron storage in astrocytes is a potential therapeutic target to lessen CNS inflammation and myelin loss in autoimmune demyelinating diseases.
39228110.summary: Mice with EAE lacking ferritin in astrocytes had milder disease, fewer inflammatory cells, less iron buildup, oxidative stress, and myelin loss in the spinal cord.

38835441.mechanism: Activates PPARβ/δ to preserve barriers and enrich Tregs
38835441.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our findings suggest that gemfibrozil, a known ligand of PPARα, preserves the integrity of BBB/BSB, enriches Tregs, and inhibits the disease process of EAE via PPARβ, but not PPARα.
38835441.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the lipid-lowering drug gemfibrozil protected the blood-brain barrier, increased regulatory T cells, and eased disease through PPARβ/δ.

38315039.mechanism: Removing STAP-1 weakens T-cell receptor signaling
38315039.conclusion_quote: Taken together, STAP-1 enhances TCR signaling and plays a role in T cell-mediated immune disorders.
38315039.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, removing the STAP-1 protein reduced T-cell activity and lessened disease symptoms, showing it fuels harmful immune attacks.

38830764.conclusion_quote: These results introduce important considerations for future TREM2-targeting approaches.
38830764.summary: In mice with Alzheimer's-like pathology, TREM2 antibodies gave little benefit, while in mice with myelin damage they slowed or disrupted repair.

38473703.mechanism: Modulates S1P1 and S1P5 receptors, reducing oxidative stress and neuronal apopto
38473703.conclusion_quote: Our data suggest that the neuroprotection of siponimod/BAF312 likely involves the relief of oxidative stress in neuronal cells.
38473703.summary: In rat and human stem-cell-derived neurons exposed to the inflammatory signal TNF-alpha, siponimod reduced cell death, likely by easing oxidative stress.

39323296.mechanism: Activates Nrf2, boosting antioxidant enzymes and suppressing inflammation
39323296.conclusion_quote: We also confirmed that 10v effectively reversed disease progression and attenuated demyelination in an experimental autoimmune encephalitis (EAE) mouse model of MS.
39323296.summary: A new compound, 10v, activated the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway, reduced inflammation, and reversed disease progression in mice with EAE.

38951694.mechanism: activates Nurr1 transcription factor to boost neuroprotective signaling
38951694.conclusion_quote: In human midbrain organoids bearing a Parkinson-driving LRRK2 mutation, a novel Nurr1 agonist rescued tyrosine hydroxylase expression highlighting the potential of the new Nurr1 modulator chemotype as lead and as a chemical tool for biological studies.
38951694.summary: In human midbrain organoids with a Parkinson's-linked LRRK2 mutation, a new Nurr1 agonist drug restored tyrosine hydroxylase, a protein needed to make dopamine.

38996070.mechanism: Promotes CCR9 expression so regulatory T cells migrate into inflamed tissue
38996070.conclusion_quote: Our work provides insights into the essential role of BAF60b in regulating Treg cell migration and its impact on inflammatory diseases.
38996070.summary: In mice with EAE and colitis, removing the BAF60b gene from regulatory T cells reduced their migration to inflamed tissue and worsened inflammation.

37646205.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that neuroinflammatory states are associated with the appearance of functionally distinct eN/CD73 glycovariants, which may play a role in the development of the reactive astrocyte phenotype.
37646205.summary: Researchers examined the CD73 enzyme in mice with EAE and in cultured astrocytes exposed to inflammatory signals, finding distinct sugar modified forms that may shape reactive astrocyte behavior.

39390606.mechanism: blocks DLL4 signaling and astrocyte reactivity
39390606.conclusion_quote: As a general conclusion, this study demonstrates that DLL4-NOTCH1 signaling is not only a key pathway in vascular development and angiogenesis, but also in the control of astrocyte reactivity during neuroinflammation.
39390606.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking the DLL4 protein with antibodies reduced inflamed astrocyte activity and improved symptoms, suggesting a possible new treatment for autoimmune demyelinating disease.

39428507.mechanism: MOG-targeted regulatory T cells induce tolerance to myelin
39428507.conclusion_quote: In summary our data suggest that MOG-CAR Tregs are a promising MS treatment option with the potential to induce long-lasting tolerance in patients.
39428507.summary: In mice with passive EAE, engineered regulatory T cells carrying a receptor that targets myelin improved disease, suggesting a new cell treatment for MS.

39563375.mechanism: Increases regulatory T cells, reduces CD4 T-cell infiltration
39563375.conclusion_quote: Our findings confirm the immunomodulatory role of IL-37 in CNS inflammation during ongoing disease, thus indicating the potential of IL-37 as an inhibitory reagent for MS therapy.
39563375.summary: In mice with EAE, a treatment with IL-37 started after disease onset produced milder disease, less myelin loss, and fewer immune cells in the brain and spinal cord.

38648385.mechanism: inhibits TAK1 shifting microglia toward M2 anti-inflammatory state
38648385.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that inhibiting TAK1 may be an effective approach for treating demyelinating diseases.
38648385.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause demyelination, the TAK1 inhibitor 5Z-7-Oxozaenol reduced myelin loss, improved movement, and shifted microglia toward a repair-supporting state.

38438357.mechanism: Blocks CTP synthesis, limiting T-cell expansion
38438357.conclusion_quote: These findings support that CTPS1 may represent a target for immune suppression.
38438357.summary: In mice, blocking the CTPS1 enzyme in T cells or with an inhibitor prevented fatal autoimmunity and reduced the severity of EAE, a mouse model of MS.

38740862.conclusion_quote: Astroglial Cx43 hemichannels represent a novel therapeutic target for chronic EAE and MS.
38740862.summary: In mice with chronic EAE, a connexin blocker that reaches the brain reduced spinal cord damage, inflammation and disability when given after symptoms began.

39404404.mechanism: Blocks kinin B1 receptor, preserving BBB tight junctions
39404404.conclusion_quote: The results show that B1 R-mediated signaling is involved in inducing molecular changes at the level of cerebral microvessels, leading to increased permeability of the BBB following neuroinflammation in EAE.
39404404.summary: In rats with EAE, a drug blocking the kinin B1 receptor reduced neurological symptoms and restored blood-brain barrier tight junction proteins and reduced leakage.

38398879.mechanism: Lowers oxidative stress and protects brain tissue
38398879.conclusion_quote: Overall, both sexes benefitted from VD supplementation, represented by significantly less cortical, neuroaxonal and oxidative damage.
38398879.summary: In rats modeling progressive MS, vitamin D supplementation reduced brain damage and oxidative stress in both sexes, with males showing the larger benefit.

38115597.mechanism: Modifies gut microbiota, represses TLR4-MyD88 inflammatory pathway
38115597.conclusion_quote: This study suggests that diosgenin plays a role in modifying gut microbiota, contributing to the alleviation of intestinal inflammation and neuroinflammation, ultimately inhibiting epilepsy progression in a PTZ-induced mouse model.
38115597.summary: In mice with seizures induced by PTZ, the natural compound diosgenin reduced seizures and brain injury by altering gut bacteria and calming inflammation.

38193859.conclusion_quote: Our study revealed a mechanism by which mural cell-macrophage interactions regulate the trafficking of CNS antigen-specific T cells to the dura.
38193859.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, blood vessel-wrapping mural cells passed cell components to dural macrophages, which limited harmful T cells reaching the protective membranes around the brain.

39210647.mechanism: Deletes lymphotoxin alpha from specific immune cell types
39210647.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our findings unveil the multifaceted involvement of lymphotoxins in EAE pathogenesis and challenge the view that lymphotoxins play a solely pathogenic role in neuroinflammation.
39210647.summary: In mice with EAE, removing lymphotoxin alpha from different immune cells had varying effects: ILC3 lymphotoxins protected, while T cell and B cell lymphotoxins promoted disease.

38237601.mechanism: blocks histone acetylation at glycolytic genes
38237601.conclusion_quote: Treatment with KAT6A small-molecule inhibitors in mouse models shows high therapeutic value for targeting KAT6A in autoimmunity.
38237601.summary: In mice with EAE, a lab model of MS, blocking the epigenetic enzyme KAT6A reduced harmful immune cell activity and disease by changing how immune cells use glucose.

39148732.mechanism: Deletion reduces dendritic cell cytokines and Th17 differentiation
39148732.conclusion_quote: Together, by regulating DC metabolism, FPR2 enhances the production of DC-derived Th17-polarizing cytokines and hence Th17 cell differentiation in the context of neuroinflammation.
39148732.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the FPR2 receptor delayed disease onset and reduced Th17 immune cells early on, but did not change severity at the peak.

38719983.mechanism: Blocks LPA1 receptor, reducing neuroinflammation and promoting oligodendrocyte d
38719983.conclusion_quote: These findings support targeting LPA1 for remyelination and encourage development of PIPE-791 for treating MS patients with advantages not seen with current immunosuppressive disease modifying therapies.
38719983.summary: In lab studies and mice with EAE, the oral drug PIPE-791 blocked the LPA1 receptor, reduced brain inflammation, promoted myelin repair, and improved visual nerve signals.

interventions: knockdown of GPR17 by adeno-associated virus
39664418.mechanism: Blocks GPR17 receptor in amygdala glutamatergic neurons
39664418.conclusion_quote: Our study finds for the first and highlights the new role of GPR17 in regulating anxiety-like behaviors and it might be a novel potential target for therapy of anxiety disorders.
39664418.summary: In mice under chronic stress, blocking or reducing GPR17 in amygdala neurons eased anxiety-like behavior, suggesting it could be a target for anxiety treatment.

37995941.mechanism: miR-23a-3p transfer targets Tbr1/Wnt signaling, promoting oligodendrocyte differ
37995941.conclusion_quote: This study provides cellular and molecular insights into the use of cell-free exosome therapy for central nervous system demyelination associated with multiple sclerosis, demonstrating its great potential for treating demyelinating and neurodegenerative diseases.
37995941.summary: Exosomes from human umbilical cord stem cells were given to mice with EAE, an MS-like model, which improved neurological function and helped the myelin coating of nerves regrow.

37581848.mechanism: Restores gut microbiota and raises short chain fatty acids
37581848.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, matrine treatment can regulate gut microbiota and metabolites and halt the progression of MS.
37581848.summary: Matrine, a herbal compound, was tested in mice with EAE, an MS model, and it eased disease by restoring gut bacteria and short chain fatty acids.

38509377.mechanism: Removes ACLY, reducing astrocyte inflammatory memory chromatin changes
38509377.conclusion_quote: In summary, these studies define an epigenetically controlled memory astrocyte subset that promotes CNS pathology in EAE and, potentially, multiple sclerosis.
38509377.summary: In mice with EAE, switching off the ACLY gene in astrocytes reduced disease, showing that inflammatory astrocyte memory helps drive damage to the nervous system.

37498431.mechanism: Removing TREM-2 blocks ZAP70/STAT3 signaling and Th17 differentiation
37498431.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, TREM-2 is a key regulator of pathogenic Th17 in EAE mice, and this sheds new light on the potential of this therapeutic target for MS.
37498431.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting Trem-2 only in T cells reduced disease activity and harmful Th17 immune cells, suggesting TREM-2 drives MS-like inflammation.

38353925.mechanism: Restores SOD1 activity, reducing oxidative stress in oligodendrocytes
38353925.conclusion_quote: Taken together, the present study revealed that arsenic protects oligodendrocytes and demyelination of corpus callosum by reversing CPZ-induced impaired SOD1 activity.
38353925.summary: In mice given cuprizone to induce demyelination, arsenic protected corpus callosum myelin and oligodendrocytes by restoring the antioxidant enzyme SOD1.

38372436.conclusion_quote: Thus, we indicated the association between non-stimuli painful perception, anxiety-like, and CNS oxidative damage in the PMS-EAE model.
38372436.summary: In mice with progressive EAE, higher levels of oxidative damage markers in the brain and spinal cord were linked to pain sensitivity, anxiety behavior, and worse clinical scores.

39103056.mechanism: Liposomes delay fingolimod partitioning into red blood cells
39103056.conclusion_quote: Thus, loading fingolimod into liposomes prevented partitioning to RBCs and associated toxicities and enabled targeted delivery.
39103056.summary: In mice with stroke-related brain inflammation, antibody-targeted fingolimod liposomes sealed the leaky blood-brain barrier better than free fingolimod and protected red blood cells.

39104416.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our data indicate that respiratory viral infection is capable of suppressing remyelination, and suggest that metabolic dysfunction of OLs is implicated in remyelination impairment.
39104416.summary: In mice given cuprizone to damage myelin, influenza A infection delayed myelin repair and changed oligodendrocyte energy metabolism in the prefrontal cortex.

37639065.conclusion_quote: These observations suggest that B. breve could provide a supplementary strategy for the treatment of multiple sclerosis by increasing antioxidant capacity and remyelination.
37639065.summary: In rats given cuprizone to damage myelin, Bifidobacterium breve reduced myelin loss and oxidative stress more than Lactobacillus casei.

39213705.mechanism: Loss blocks progenitor differentiation into oligodendrocytes
39213705.conclusion_quote: Our data support the idea that OPCs are the major cell sources for myelin regeneration, suggesting that targeting the activation of OPCs and promoting their differentiation to boost new OLs production is critical for therapeutic intervention for demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis (MS).
39213705.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, deleting Myrf from oligodendrocyte progenitor cells impaired remyelination and left lasting anxiety, motor and memory deficits.

38452827.mechanism: Radiolabeled probe binds myelin, enabling SPECT imaging
38452827.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, [ 123 I]BO-2 demonstrated the fundamental characteristics of a myelin imaging probe for SPECT.
38452827.summary: Researchers tested four radioactive iodine tracers for SPECT scans of myelin in mice, and BO-2 best distinguished white matter from gray matter and dropped in demyelinated lesions.

39462277.mechanism: Depletes butyrate-producing gut bacteria via bacteriocins
39462277.conclusion_quote: Our data highlight a potential mechanism for reduced SCFAs and their producers in MS through depletion by other members of the gut microbiome, demonstrating that interactions between microbiota can impact CNS autoimmunity in a diet-dependent manner.
39462277.summary: In mice with EAE, colonization by L. reuteri worsened disease by depleting butyrate-producing gut bacteria, and extra dietary fiber reversed this harmful effect.

39147172.mechanism: Bacterial metabolite activates LPA3 receptor, reducing neuroinflammation
39147172.conclusion_quote: Altogether, these data suggest that ADS024 and its LPA3 agonism activity should be investigated further as a possible treatment for diseases with a neuroinflammatory component.
39147172.summary: In mice with MS-like EAE and other neurological disease models, an oral bacterial product from Bacillus velezensis improved motor, breathing and immune measures, partly through the LPA3 receptor.

38303097.conclusion_quote: These findings implicate the inner plexiform layer as an early imaging biomarker of excitotoxic retinal degeneration, whereas caution is warranted when interpreting the ganglion cell complex combining retinal nerve fiber layer, ganglion cell layer, and inner plexiform layer thicknesses in conventional OCT measures.
38303097.summary: In rats given a toxic dose of NMDA into the eye, deep learning analysis of scans showed the inner plexiform layer thinned first, while the nerve fiber layer briefly thickened.

37914099.mechanism: Removing GSDMD reduces inflammatory cell death in macrophages and oligodendrocyt
37914099.conclusion_quote: GSDMD activation in CNS macrophages and oligodendrocytes contributes to inflammatory demyelination and neuroaxonal injury, offering mechanistic and potential therapeutic insights into P-MS pathogenesis.
37914099.summary: In mice exposed to cuprizone, removing the GSDMD gene reduced inflammatory demyelination and nerve fiber damage in the brain's corpus callosum.

37619413.mechanism: Shifts microglia to M2 and calms inflammatory signaling
37619413.conclusion_quote: Our results indicate that Hydroxyfasudil may be a prospective treatment for MS.
37619413.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the drug hydroxyfasudil reduced symptoms, immune cell invasion, and inflammation while protecting the blood brain barrier.

37217574.mechanism: Modulates lymphocyte trafficking and fumarate NRF2 signalling
37217574.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, hyperpolarized MRS metabolic imaging of [1- 13 C]pyruvate detects immunological responses to disease-modifying therapies in MS.
37217574.summary: In mice with a multiple sclerosis-like model, fingolimod and dimethyl fumarate reduced brain immune activity, and a special metabolic MRI scan detected this change.

37915090.mechanism: Inhibits heparanase, preserving barrier integrity and reducing lymphocyte migrat
37915090.conclusion_quote: Together these results suggest that Tet-29 modulates, rather than abolishes, trafficking across central nervous system barriers.
37915090.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, the heparanase-blocking compound Tet-29 reduced immune cell entry into the brain and lowered disease severity.

38248227.mechanism: Inhibits inflammation, oxidative stress and apoptosis
38248227.conclusion_quote: The current study demonstrated a neuroprotective effect for VA against the Cup-induced demyelinating rat model.
38248227.summary: In rats given cuprizone to damage myelin, vanillic acid improved nerve conduction and reduced demyelination, inflammation, oxidative stress and cell death.

37187004.mechanism: miR-485 binds STAT3, reducing Th17 cell generation
37187004.conclusion_quote: Overall, miR-485 exert vital functions in Th17 generation and EAE pathogenesis.
37187004.summary: In mice with EAE, raising levels of the microRNA miR-485 lowered inflammatory Th17 cells and eased disease, while lowering it worsened symptoms.

37394105.mechanism: Blocks AQP4, reducing astrocyte, microglia and inflammasome activity
37394105.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, the results draw the attention to the role of AQP4 in the cuprizone model of MS.
37394105.summary: In mice fed cuprizone to mimic MS, blocking the AQP4 water channel with TGN020 reduced inflammation and nerve damage and improved movement.

37090733.mechanism: removes T-cell co-stimulation, impairing virus clearance
37090733.conclusion_quote: Therefore, the clinical outcome largely depends on the time point of the CD28-knockout during development of the immune system.
37090733.summary: In mice infected with Theiler's virus, a model of MS, deleting CD28 caused virus persistence and worse outcomes, with effects depending on when the gene was removed.

38085147.mechanism: favors regulatory T cells over Th17 cells
38085147.conclusion_quote: This study provides further evidence of the anti-inflammatory effects of calcitriol and its role in attenuating EAE.
38085147.summary: Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, was given to mice with EAE and reduced disease symptoms and inflammatory signals in immune cells.

37332201.conclusion_quote: In keeping with this, we revealed that CSF L-Asp levels were positively correlated with those of L-Glu, highlighting the convergent variation of these two excitatory amino acids under inflammatory synaptopathy occurring in MS.
37332201.summary: In mice with EAE and in MS patients, levels of the excitatory amino acid aspartate were lower in spinal fluid and tracked with glutamate and inflammation markers.

37949310.mechanism: Not applicable, describes protein changes only
37949310.conclusion_quote: This study provides insights into the similarities and differences in the responses of these regions in two distinct demyelinating models.
37949310.summary: Researchers compared protein levels in brain and spinal cord tissue of mice fed cuprizone or with EAE, finding Orosomucoid-1 changed in both models.

37558696.mechanism: Neutralizes Nogo-A, reducing signaling and preserving spinal cord myelin
37558696.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our data show the feasibility of olfactory mucosa-directed administration for the delivery of therapeutic antibodies targeting CNS antigens in EAE mice.
37558696.summary: In mice with EAE, an antibody delivered through the nose reached the brain and spinal cord, improving motor symptoms and preserving myelin.

37915599.mechanism: Suppresses gut trypsin activity, preserving intestinal barrier and Lactobacilli
37915599.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that the interaction between intestinal PAR2 and trypsin may be a key modulator of intestinal permeability and disease severity during EAE.
37915599.summary: In mice with EAE, oral vancomycin preserved the gut lining, lowered gut trypsin activity, and reduced disease severity.

37897611.mechanism: Modulates miRNA expression, suppressing Th1/Th17 and promoting Treg responses
37897611.conclusion_quote: Our findings suggest that BM-MSCs administration might change expression patterns of miRNAs and downstream interactions followed by immune system modulation.
37897611.summary: In mice with EAE, bone marrow stem cells reduced disease severity and inflammation by altering microRNA levels and calming harmful immune responses.

37591119.mechanism: Inhibits AP1, reducing Th1 and Th17 cell differentiation
37591119.conclusion_quote: The results suggest that TPN10518 reduces the production of Th1 and Th17 cells through inhibition of AP1 to alleviate the severity of EAE disease.
37591119.summary: In mice with EAE, a new artemisinin-derived small molecule called TPN10518 reduced immune cell infiltration into the brain and spinal cord and eased symptoms by blocking AP1.

37629171.mechanism: Modulates S1P receptors, trapping lymphocytes and reducing microglial activation
37629171.conclusion_quote: However, it did not demonstrate a significant impact on neurodegeneration, spinal volume, or lesion volume in the TMEV mouse model.
37629171.summary: In mice with a virus-induced MS model, siponimod reduced enlargement of brain fluid spaces and may have eased inflammation, but it did not slow nerve tissue loss or spinal cord shrinkage.

37455566.mechanism: Not applicable, describes astrocyte gene signatures only
37455566.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, we detected highly dynamic astroglial transcriptomic signatures in the cuprizone model, which reflects excessive communication among glia cells and highlights different astrocyte functions during neurodegeneration and regeneration.
37455566.summary: In mice fed cuprizone to damage myelin, researchers tracked astrocyte gene activity during damage and repair, finding astrocytes shift from inflammatory to repair supporting states.

36731819.mechanism: suppresses microglial NLRP3 inflammasome activation, reducing neuroinflammation
36731819.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our findings have demonstrated that ICA, as pleiotropic agent, prevents EAE-induced MS by improving demyelination and neuron loss, which interferes with the neuroinflammation via microglial NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
36731819.summary: Mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, were given icariin, a natural flavonoid, which reduced symptoms, nerve damage, and brain inflammation.

37770161.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that microglial depletion exacerbates axonal damage and motor dysfunction in CPZ model mice.
37770161.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause demyelination, depleting microglia with the drug PLX3397 worsened movement problems and increased nerve fiber damage.

37084732.mechanism: Blocks S1P receptors and lowers very-long-chain fatty acid levels
37084732.conclusion_quote: Moreover, simultaneous use of bezafibrate and fingolimod synergizes to improve EAE, suggesting that lowering VLCFA and S1P is a treatment avenue for MS.
37084732.summary: In fruit flies and mice with EAE, the drugs fingolimod and bezafibrate reduced inflammation caused by excess very long chain fatty acids.

36939622.mechanism: Alters gut microbiota and modulates immune cell populations
36939622.conclusion_quote: Overall, our data suggest that in C57Bl6/J mice, an FRD modulates the gut microbiota and immune system without significantly impacting myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein 35-55/CFA-induced EAE.
36939622.summary: In mice with EAE, a diet rich in fructose altered gut bacteria and immune cells but did not significantly worsen disease.

37088262.conclusion_quote: These findings support the concept that respiratory bacteria may contribute to the pathophysiology of CNS autoimmunity by modulating pathogenicity in crucial T-cell subsets that orchestrate neuroinflammation.
37088262.summary: In mice with EAE, respiratory bacteria Moraxella catarrhalis and Klebsiella pneumoniae worsened disease and increased inflammatory GM-CSF producing T cells in the brain and spinal cord.

37350546.mechanism: Targets queuine tRNA ribosyltransferase to alter tRNA modification
37350546.conclusion_quote: Several active 7-deazaguanines emerged, together with a structure-activity relationship involving the necessity for a flexible alkyl chain of fixed length.
37350546.summary: Researchers tested a library of queuine analogues in mice with EAE, an MS model, and found several compounds that were active in treating the disease.

36945189.conclusion_quote: These data support the future clinical translation of this next generation modified heparin as a treatment for CNS diseases with active immune system involvement.
36945189.summary: In mice with EAE and cuprizone-induced demyelination, a modified heparin called LS-mHep7 sped recovery and reduced inflammation in EAE but did not improve myelin repair.

38077336.conclusion_quote: However, this pathway is not altered in the olfactory bulb of EAE mice.
38077336.summary: In mice with EAE, the cAMP signaling that astrocytes in the olfactory bulb trigger through adenosine A2A receptors was no different from that in healthy mice.

37400950.mechanism: Blocks FGFR signalling, reducing immune cell proliferation
37400950.conclusion_quote: This proof of concept study demonstrates the therapeutic potential of targeting FGFRs in a disease model of multiple sclerosis.
37400950.summary: In mice with EAE, the oral drug infigratinib reduced first disease episodes, lowered spinal cord inflammation, and increased myelin repair.

37212607.mechanism: blocks GM-CSF pathway, reducing survival of myeloid cells
37212607.conclusion_quote: Therefore, GM-CSF suppression is a possible therapeutic approach in inflammatory CNS diseases with relapse, such as MS.
37212607.summary: In mice with transfer EAE, blocking the GM-CSF signal reduced the survival of immune cells in the spinal cord and suppressed pain-triggered relapses.

37571246.mechanism: Antioxidant effects reduce oxidative stress and neuronal damage
37571246.conclusion_quote: Our data thus show a positive effect of VD on cellular features of cortical pathology in our animal model, presumably due to protection against reactive oxygen species.
37571246.summary: In rats with a model of progressive multiple sclerosis-like cortical damage, vitamin D supplementation reduced brain inflammation, nerve cell death, oxidative stress, and blood markers of nerve injury.

37958787.mechanism: modulates innate immune cells in the CNS
37958787.conclusion_quote: Thus, exercise training is capable of attenuating the disease course even in established secondary progressive EAE, potentially via modulation of the innate immune compartment.
37958787.summary: Endurance exercise on running wheels, started at disease onset, eased symptoms in mice with progressive EAE, a model of MS, and altered innate immune cells.

36883849.mechanism: deletes miR-155 in specific immune cell types to test their roles
36883849.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these data show that although miR-155 is highly expressed in most infiltrating immune cells, miR-155 has distinct roles and requirements depending on the cell type, and we have demonstrated this using the gold standard conditional KO approach.
36883849.summary: Researchers deleted the microRNA-155 gene in specific immune cell types of mice with EAE, finding that removing it in T cells or dendritic cells reduced disease, but not in macrophages.

37511812.mechanism: Microbial antigen immunization triggers IgG4 response and worsens EAE
37511812.conclusion_quote: These findings provide evidence suggesting a potential link between MAP and the development or exacerbation of MS, particularly in a subgroup of MS patients with elevated serum IgG4 levels.
37511812.summary: Researchers found higher IgG4 antibodies against a bacterial peptide in MS patients, and mice immunized with it developed worse EAE, a mouse model of MS.

36732292.mechanism: removes pathogenic immunoglobulin G from CSF
36732292.conclusion_quote: Our findings suggest that the clinical and pathological features of primary progressive multiple sclerosis are antibody-mediated and pathogenically distinct from relapsing-remitting and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
36732292.summary: In mice, cerebrospinal fluid from primary progressive MS patients caused motor disability and spinal cord damage, and this effect was reduced by removing its immunoglobulin G antibodies.

37565654.mechanism: competes with virus for sialylated integrin binding, reducing viral entry
37565654.conclusion_quote: These results show that the chronic encephalomyelitis virus utilizes sialylated integrins as cell surface receptors, leading to cellular tropism to evade pDC activation.
37565654.summary: In mice infected with Theiler's virus, a protein from the integrin family reduced viral replication, and the virus was found to use sialylated integrins to enter cells.

36921064.mechanism: knockdown blocks interferon gamma signaling in choroid plexus
36921064.conclusion_quote: Above all, we discovered that IFN-γR1-mediated IFN-γ signaling in the CP was a vital pathway in the pathological process of EAE.
36921064.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking the immune signal interferon gamma in the choroid plexus, a brain barrier tissue, reduced disease severity and immune cell entry into the brain.

36458588.mechanism: blocks neutrophil accumulation in lymph nodes, reducing CD4 T cell expansion
36458588.conclusion_quote: Collectively, this study demonstrates the key role of neutrophils in the quantitative regulation of antigen-specific CD4 + T cell expansion in lymph nodes, and the counter-regulatory role of TLR signaling in this process.
36458588.summary: In mice with EAE, a TLR9 agonist reduced neutrophil buildup in lymph nodes and T cell expansion, slowing disease in mice lacking certain regulatory immune cells.

37263067.mechanism: Autophagy suppresses microglial inflammation through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway
37263067.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, this study substantiated that autophagy induced by AXL inhibited the inflammatory response of microglia and alleviated symptoms of EAE.
37263067.summary: In mice with EAE, knocking out the AXL gene reduced microglial autophagy and worsened inflammation and demyelination.

36745025.mechanism: Induces anti-inflammatory IL-10 T cells and M2 microglia
36745025.conclusion_quote: Our data provide new insights into the cell-mediated and humoral immune mechanisms underlying BCG vaccine-induced neuroprotection, potentially useful for developing better strategies for the treatment of MS.
36745025.summary: In mice with EAE, a BCG Tokyo-172 vaccine given before disease onset protected against paralysis mainly in younger mice, by calming immune responses in the spleen and brain cells.

36964399.mechanism: shifts microglia toward anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype
36964399.conclusion_quote: Results indicate that treatment applied to experimental animals influences the microglia phenotype, promoting differentiation towards M2 cells.
36964399.summary: In rats with EAE, stem cell transplantation with cyclophosphamide shifted brain immune cells toward a calming M2 form, though not all markers changed.

37071991.mechanism: boosts oligodendrocyte precursor cell differentiation into myelin-forming cells
37071991.conclusion_quote: These data indicate that the contribution of surviving oligodendrocytes to myelin recovery in the inflamed mammalian CNS is minor and inhibited by distinct remyelination brakes.
37071991.summary: In mice with a cortical MS-like lesion model, surviving oligodendrocytes rarely made new myelin, and drugs boosting precursor cells did not increase this repair.

37378907.mechanism: Stimulates aromatase expression and reduces spinal cord inflammation
37378907.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, naringenin could provide long-term beneficial effects even in prophylactic use due to stimulating aromatase expression, but it could not prevent or eliminate the EAE model's lesions completely.
37378907.summary: In mice with EAE, the flavonoid naringenin reduced clinical signs and spinal cord inflammation when given before or after disease onset, while boosting aromatase.

37132422.mechanism: Intermittent low oxygen reduces inflammation and promotes remyelination
37132422.conclusion_quote: Collectively, this supports a role for AIH as a novel non-invasive therapy to enhance CNS repair and alter disease course following demyelination and holds promise as a neuroregenerative MS strategy.
37132422.summary: In mice with EAE, brief cycles of low oxygen breathing started at peak disease improved symptoms, reduced inflammation, and promoted myelin repair.

37894952.mechanism: blocks histamine H4 receptor, rebalancing T cells
37894952.conclusion_quote: Therefore, the HR4 antagonist positively affected the course of EAE by modulating the signaling of transcription factors.
37894952.summary: In mice with EAE, a histamine H4 receptor blocking drug given daily slowed disease and shifted immune T cells toward calming types.

37246862.conclusion_quote: The use of an encephalitogen (e.g., MOG35-55) emulsified in an adjuvant containing M. paratuberculosis in the formulation may be an alternative and validated method to activate dendritic cells for priming myelin epitope-specific CD4 + T-cells during the induction phase of EAE.
37246862.summary: In mice with EAE, an adjuvant containing Mycobacterium paratuberculosis triggered earlier and more severe disease than standard Freund's adjuvant, offering an alternative way to induce the model.

37003487.mechanism: thyroid hormone boosts brain myelin lipid synthesis
37003487.conclusion_quote: Labeling of blood 24-OHC has potential as a non-invasive marker of brain de novo cholesterol synthesis and breakdown rates in demyelinating conditions.
37003487.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause brain demyelination, thyroid hormone T3 increased myelin lipid synthesis during recovery, and blood 24-OHC levels closely tracked these brain changes.

36521687.mechanism: Macrophage-derived exosomes deliver resveratrol to microglia, reducing inflammat
36521687.conclusion_quote: These findings suggested the feasibility and efficacy of engineered RSV&Exo administration for MS, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for CNS diseases.
36521687.summary: In mice with an MS model, intranasal resveratrol-loaded macrophage exosomes reduced nervous system and body-wide inflammation and improved clinical signs of the disease.

37679570.mechanism: Induces antigen-specific T-cell tolerance via PD-1 and CD276
37679570.conclusion_quote: Our findings show that pGal-antigen therapy invokes mechanisms of immune tolerance to resolve antigen-specific inflammatory T-cell responses and suggest that the therapy may be applicable across autoimmune diseases.
37679570.summary: In mice with EAE, a sugar-coated antigen therapy trained harmful T cells to stop attacking the target antigen, calming inflammation without broad immune suppression.

37828379.mechanism: PGLYRP1 loss impairs myeloid antigen presentation
37828379.conclusion_quote: These results highlight PGLYRP1 as a promising target for immunotherapy that, when targeted, elicits a potent antitumor immune response while protecting against some forms of tissue inflammation and autoimmunity.
37828379.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the Pglyrp1 gene protected against disease by weakening myeloid cells' ability to activate T cells.

37417746.mechanism: blocks STAP-2 binding to CD3ζ ITAMs
37417746.conclusion_quote: It is likely that iSP2 is a novel immunomodulatory tool that modulates STAP-2-mediated activation of TCR signaling and represses the progression of autoimmune diseases.
37417746.summary: In mice with EAE, a peptide that blocks the STAP-2 protein from switching on T cells reduced immune responses and disease progression.

37452099.mechanism: Deleting Pparα increases IKKα, boosting Th17 cell development
37452099.conclusion_quote: Overall, our data indicate that Pparα may serve as a potential therapeutic target for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.
37452099.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the Pparα gene increased harmful Th17 immune cells and made the disease worse.

35147137.mechanism: No treatment tested, only describes receptor expression
35147137.conclusion_quote: This study provides additional evidence of galanin involvement in EAE pathophysiology, but this has to be further investigated.
35147137.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, spinal cord galanin receptor GalR1 levels were lower than in controls, while GalR2 and GalR3 were unchanged.

37153635.mechanism: Reduces glial, T-cell and macrophage activity, oxidative stress
37153635.conclusion_quote: The neuroprotective effects of melatonin in cuprizone-treated mice have been realized through an improvement of the brain cell composition and oxidative stress factors and functioning of bone marrow and thymus.
37153635.summary: In cuprizone-treated young and aging mice, melatonin reduced brain inflammatory cells and oxidative stress, protected neurons, and improved behavior.

37438826.mechanism: Reduces microglial activation, cytokines and immune cell infiltration
37438826.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our results highlight the future use of FTY720 as a direct anti-inflammatory treatment against microglial activation and psychosis.
37438826.summary: In mice given cuprizone, a demyelinating agent that causes brain inflammation, fingolimod reduced drug hypersensitivity and lowered microglial activation and inflammation.

37638040.mechanism: Binds monocytes, blocking T cell entry into CNS
37638040.conclusion_quote: We show that M019 effectively reduced clinical symptoms when given either pre- or post-symptom onset compared to vehicle treated EAE induced mice.
37638040.summary: In mice with EAE, a designed immune protein called M019 reduced symptoms whether given before or after symptoms began.

36849508.mechanism: Blocks Th17 cells, promotes Treg cells
36849508.conclusion_quote: These results indicate that itaconate is a crucial metabolic regulator for Th17/Treg cell balance and could be a potential therapeutic agent for autoimmune diseases.
36849508.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the immune metabolite itaconate shifted T cells away from inflammatory Th17 cells toward calming Treg cells, which eased disease.

36857453.mechanism: induces apoptosis of encephalitogenic T cells via perivascular F4/80 cells
36857453.conclusion_quote: Our study reveals alternative mechanisms that explain how cognate antigen suppresses CNS inflammation and may be applicable for effectively and safely treating demyelinating diseases.
36857453.summary: In mice with EAE, an injectable myelin antigen called MMPt suppressed disease and CNS inflammation without major side effects by causing attacking T cells to die.

36692902.mechanism: Reduces overactive astrocyte calcium signaling to inflammatory cytokines
36692902.conclusion_quote: We show the efficacy of GO to revert these dynamic changes in astrocytic reactivity to CKs, and we translate this potential in an animal model of immune-mediated neuroinflammatory disease.
36692902.summary: In an animal model of EAE, graphene oxide nanosheets calmed overactive astrocytes and eased the immune-driven nerve inflammation.

36980209.mechanism: Blocks L1 retrotransposon, reducing neurotoxic T cell accumulation in CNS
36980209.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our data highlight a critical contribution of new microglia subsets as a neuroinflammatory hub in immune-mediated neurodegeneration.
36980209.summary: In mice with EAE, an L1 inhibitor eased neurodegenerative symptoms and reduced harmful Eomes-expressing T cells in the central nervous system.

38090669.mechanism: activates kappa opioid receptors, reducing immune cell infiltration
38090669.conclusion_quote: This study indicates that KOR agonists can be used in combination with fingolimod and dimethyl fumarate with the nalfurafine-fingolimod combination providing enhanced benefits.
38090669.summary: In mice with EAE, nalfurafine combined with fingolimod improved recovery, reduced relapses, lowered immune cell entry into the spinal cord and increased myelination.

36543959.mechanism: Represses MAFB to favor dendritic cell fate
36543959.conclusion_quote: These findings provide information about the molecular control of monocyte fate decision and identify ETV6 as a therapeutic target to redirect monocyte differentiation in inflammatory disorders.
36543959.summary: Deleting Etv6 in monocytes reduced dendritic cell formation and disease severity in mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis.

37598833.conclusion_quote: These results confirmed the use of mouse hippocampal neuron cultures as a model to study neuronal responses after TMEV infection, particularly in the formation of spine density.
37598833.summary: In cultured mouse brain neurons, the Theiler's virus replicated, reduced neuron survival, and lowered spine density, with a mutant lacking the L* protein reducing spine density most.

37364629.mechanism: chemically triggered death of optic nerve oligodendrocytes causes demyelination
37364629.conclusion_quote: These results show that a partial demyelination of a subpopulation of RGC axons disrupts optic nerve function and affects the organization of the retinal network.
37364629.summary: In mice where optic nerve oligodendrocytes were chemically destroyed, partial myelin loss disrupted nerve signaling and reduced key retinal cell types, showing demyelination affects upstream vision circuits.

36787309.mechanism: Gut metabolite shifts reduce T cell fitness
36787309.conclusion_quote: Our study demonstrates a newly emerging role for AHR in mediating the interdependence between T lymphocytes and the microbiota, while simultaneously identifying new potential molecular targets for the treatment of MS and other autoimmune diseases.
36787309.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the AHR receptor from T cells reduced disease by changing gut chemicals that T cells need to survive.

36950280.mechanism: Inhibits SARM1 NAD+ hydrolase, reducing axon degeneration
36950280.conclusion_quote: Our studies therefore suggest that SARM1 inhibition by local ASO delivery or AAV-mediated CRISPR is a promising neuroprotective gene therapy strategy for traumatic and glaucomatous optic neuropathies but not for demyelinating optic neuritis.
36950280.summary: In mice, blocking the SARM1 gene protected nerve cells in glaucoma and optic nerve injury models but not in an EAE model of optic neuritis.

37540445.mechanism: promotes microglial switch from M1 to M2 phenotype
37540445.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that 2ccPA treatment suppresses behavioral abnormalities by promoting a microglial phenotypic switch from M1 to M2 in MRL/lpr mice.
37540445.summary: In a mouse model of lupus brain symptoms, a cyclic phosphatidic acid treatment shifted brain immune cells toward a healing state and reduced depressive behavior.

37719372.mechanism: Inhibits IL-17A production and glycolysis in splenic cells
37719372.conclusion_quote: Our results revealed that aureane-type sesquiterpene tetraketides are a novel class of immunomodulators with IL-17A inhibitory activity, and hold great promise applications in treating IL-17A-mediated immune diseases.
37719372.summary: In mice with EAE, a fungal compound that blocks the inflammatory signal IL-17A reduced immune-driven tissue damage, suggesting possible treatments for immune diseases.

37120788.mechanism: Loss of progranulin alters microglia, impairing myelin repair
37120788.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our data support that PGRN deficiency leads to sex-dependent alterations in microglia with subsequent myelination defects.
37120788.summary: In mice, removing progranulin made males show worse demyelination and microglia overactivity after cuprizone, with slower myelin repair in both sexes.

36493975.mechanism: severs vagus nerve gut-brain signaling link
36493975.conclusion_quote: Together, these data suggest that CPZ produces demyelination in the brain through the gut-microbiota-brain axis via the subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve.
36493975.summary: In cuprizone-fed mice, cutting the vagus nerve below the diaphragm reduced brain demyelination and microglial activation, and improved gut bacteria and blood metabolites.

36630481.mechanism: blocks common gamma chain cytokine signaling, reducing pathogenic T cell respons
36630481.conclusion_quote: By demonstrating that broad inhibition of γc cytokine signaling with REGN7257 protects from immune-mediated disorders, our data provide evidence of γc cytokines as key drivers of pathogenic T cell responses, offering a potential strategy for the management of T cell-mediated diseases.
36630481.summary: In mice with multiple sclerosis models, an antibody called REGN7257 that blocks common gamma chain cytokine signaling reduced harmful T cell activity and disease.

38269118.conclusion_quote: Their pattern was altered in neurodegenerative models including the cuprizone-induced demyelination model in mice as well as in the Royal College of Surgeons (RCS -/- ) rats.
38269118.summary: Researchers compared spontaneous electrical rhythms of the retina, recorded by eye tests, across mice, rats, humans, and zebrafish, and found altered rhythms in demyelinated mice.

35551129.mechanism: Blocks C6-C5 interaction, preventing membrane attack complex
35551129.conclusion_quote: CP010 is a promising complement C6 inhibitor that prevents MAC formation.
35551129.summary: In human C6 transgenic rats with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, a humanized antibody called CP010 blocked membrane attack complex formation and reduced relapses.

36482709.mechanism: Activates NRF2 pathway to block ferroptosis lipid peroxidation
36482709.conclusion_quote: DMF inhibits ferroptosis by activating the NRF2/SLC7A11/HO-1 axis and exerts a protective effect against hepatic IRI.
36482709.summary: In mice with liver injury from restored blood flow and in mouse liver cells, dimethyl fumarate reduced iron-driven cell death by activating NRF2, protecting the liver. This is not an MS study.

37676734.conclusion_quote: These findings support a pathogenic role for autoreactive anti-axonal and anti-neuronal CD8+ T cells in MS progression.
37676734.summary: In mice with induced demyelination, immune cells that recognize neurons entered the brain and damaged nerve fibers, suggesting a role in MS progression.

36106568.mechanism: reduces microglia activation and IL-6/IL-1β cytokines, raises BDNF
36106568.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest the immune system plays an crucial role in cognitive alterations in schizophrenia and highlight the potential of immunomodulatory strategies to improve cognitive deficits in schizophrenia.
36106568.summary: In rats given phencyclidine to mimic schizophrenia, the MS drug fingolimod improved memory and learning, restored brain cell growth, and reduced inflammation.

37744334.conclusion_quote: Overall, our results suggest a novel physiological function of ERG1 in the processes of differentiation and selection of lymphoid precursors, paving the way to further studies aimed at defining the expression and role of ERG1 channels in immune-based pathologies in addition to that during lymphocyte neoplastic transformation.
37744334.summary: In mice with EAE, immune cell precursors in bone marrow and thymus showed higher levels of the ERG1 potassium channel, which helps drive activation signals in lymphocytes.

37720086.mechanism: Removing Ddx54 causes adult myelin sheath breakdown
37720086.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrate that Ddx54 is indispensable for myelin homeostasis, and they provide a demyelinating disease model based on intrinsic disintegration of adult myelin.
37720086.summary: In mice, deleting the Ddx54 gene from oligodendrocytes caused adult myelin breakdown, nerve loss, and early death, creating a model of demyelinating disease.

37373466.mechanism: Ddr1 loss disrupts ERK signaling and oligodendrocyte differentiation
37373466.conclusion_quote: Taken together, the current study described, for the first time, the role of Ddr1 in myelin development and repair in the CNS, providing a novel molecule target for the treatment of demyelinating diseases.
37373466.summary: In mice, removing the Ddr1 gene slowed myelin formation and impaired myelin repair after lysolecithin-induced nerve damage, showing Ddr1 helps build and restore myelin.

36221192.mechanism: delivers disease antigen to induce antigen-specific T-cell tolerance
36221192.conclusion_quote: The effect of Ag loading and dosing on in vitro and in vivo immune regulation provide useful insights for translating Ag-carrier systems for the clinical treatment of immune disorders.
36221192.summary: In mice with EAE and delayed-type hypersensitivity, nanoparticles carrying a disease-relevant antigen induced tolerance only when antigen loading and particle dose were high enough.

37669365.mechanism: Removing ELOVL6 shifts phagocytes toward repair
37669365.conclusion_quote: These findings indicate that targeting ELOVL6 activity may be an effective strategy to stimulate CNS repair in MS and other neurodegenerative diseases.
37669365.summary: In mice and brain slice cultures, removing the Elovl6 gene reduced inflammatory foam cells and boosted myelin repair after demyelination.

36803190.mechanism: Knock-in of AD-risk TREM2 variant alters microglial response
36803190.conclusion_quote: The Trem2 R47H NSS mouse is a valuable model that can be used to investigate age-dependent effects of the AD-risk R47H mutation on TREM2 and microglial function including its effects on plaque development, microglial-plaque interaction, production of a unique interferon signature and associated tissue damage.
36803190.summary: In mice modeling Alzheimer's plaques, a human TREM2 risk variant reduced microglia near plaques and increased nerve damage and synapse loss over time.

36786572.mechanism: blocks CD39 enzyme that converts ATP to adenosine
36786572.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these data suggest that EBV + B cell lymphomas exploit ectonucleotidase activity to circumvent ATP-mediated inflammation and cell death.
36786572.summary: In mice with human immune cells and Epstein Barr virus lymphoma, blocking the CD39 enzyme prolonged survival, lowered tumor burden, and increased inflammatory immune responses. This study does not concern multiple sclerosis.

37663127.mechanism: Reduces astrogliosis and microgliosis, lowering inflammation at lesions
37663127.conclusion_quote: Our data indicate that NAM influences astrocytes and microglia directly, in favor of the remyelination process by promoting a less inflammatory environment.
37663127.summary: In mice with lysolecithin induced demyelination, nicotinamide, a vitamin B3 derivative, increased myelin production and reduced inflammatory astrocytes and microglia at the lesion site.

35662227.mechanism: activates NR4A1 receptor, reducing Th1/Th17 inflammation
35662227.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that the NR4A1 agonist Csn-B can alleviate nerve injury after EAE induction, and, therefore, may be useful as a potential treatment for multiple sclerosis.
35662227.summary: Mice with EAE, an MS model, given the NR4A1 agonist cytosporone B by mouth had milder symptoms and less brain and spinal inflammation.

interventions: phenethyl ester derivative of rosmarinic acid (PERA)
36183900.mechanism: Reduces inflammatory cytokines and nitric oxide production
36183900.conclusion_quote: Our results clearly imply that PERA possesses anti-encephalitogenic properties.
36183900.summary: In rats with EAE, an animal model of MS, a modified rosmarinic acid compound shortened disease and lowered inflammatory signals, suggesting possible value for multiple sclerosis treatment.

35250482.mechanism: Not applicable, descriptive study of myelin damage
35250482.conclusion_quote: This remarkable resemblance of ultrastructural myelin characteristics in multiple sclerosis and the cuprizone animal model suggests that the cuprizone model is a valuable tool to study early pathologies during lesion formation.
35250482.summary: In the cuprizone animal model, a toxin that damages oligodendrocytes, myelin developed vacuoles and axons swelled, resembling early MS lesions.

35277421.mechanism: Blocks dendritic cell IL-6 release via AMPK
35277421.conclusion_quote: Overall, our study elucidated the key role of chlorzoxazone in regulating EAE pathogenesis and suggested that it might be used as a new drug for MS patients.
35277421.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the muscle relaxant chlorzoxazone reduced symptoms, demyelination and immune cell activity by lowering IL-6 released from dendritic cells.

35091079.conclusion_quote: In summary, we were able to detect evidence of altered CCO metabolism during cuprizone exposure, consistent with a mitochondrial defect.
35091079.summary: In mice fed cuprizone to induce demyelination, researchers measured brain oxygen use and found reduced metabolism and oxygenation that recovered after the toxin was stopped.

35259641.mechanism: Disrupts gut microbiota, altering offspring immune development
35259641.conclusion_quote: Taken together, this study suggests that antibiotic treatment during pregnancy and lactation in dams might affect the development of the immune system in male and female offspring in adulthood.
35259641.summary: In mice, antibiotics given to mothers during pregnancy and nursing worsened EAE symptoms and inflammatory signals in their adult offspring.

36029715.mechanism: Nanoparticle-delivered fumarate reduces immune cell infiltration and lymphopenia
36029715.conclusion_quote: DMF incorporated in SLNs was as effective as free DMF in reducing the clinical scores of the animals, but with reduced administrations when given subcutaneously.
36029715.summary: In mice with EAE, dimethyl fumarate packed into fat based nanoparticles and given under the skin worked as well as oral dimethyl fumarate while needing fewer doses.

35348816.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway, reduces oxidative stress and apoptosis
35348816.conclusion_quote: Taken together, the present study demonstrated that magnolol has significant neuroprotective properties in EAE via inhibition of oxidative stress.
35348816.summary: Magnolol given daily to mice with EAE, a model of MS, reduced oxidative stress and nerve damage, improving clinical signs and motor function.

35947794.mechanism: Inhibits HDAC3, dampening microglia and P2X7R/STAT3/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammation
35947794.conclusion_quote: These findings demonstrated that RFFP966 alleviated the inflammatory response and exerted a neuroprotective effect possibly by modulating P2X7R/STAT3/NF-κB65/NLRP3 signaling pathways.
35947794.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, the drug RGFP966 reduced brain inflammation, protected white matter, and improved neurological behavior.

33837066.mechanism: Blocks lymphocyte exit from lymph nodes
33837066.conclusion_quote: The combination of MRI and 18 F-FAraG PET enables detection of inflammatory demyelination and T cell infiltration in an MS mouse model, providing a new way to evaluate lesion heterogeneity during disease progression and after DMT.
33837066.summary: In mice with an MS model, a PET scan that tracks T cells plus MRI detected inflammation, and fingolimod reduced T cells and prevented motor problems.

35681468.mechanism: Removing tenascin-C or tenascin-R increases myelin sheath thickness
35681468.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that the fine-tuning of myelin regeneration is regulated by the major tenascin proteins of the CNS.
35681468.summary: In mice given cuprizone to strip myelin, removing tenascin-C or tenascin-R genes made regenerated myelin sheaths thicker and increased oligodendrocyte precursor cell numbers.

35353625.mechanism: blocks CSF-1 signaling, depleting inflammatory microglia and monocytes
35353625.conclusion_quote: Our findings suggest that targeting CSF-1 could be effective in ameliorating MS pathology, while preserving the homeostatic functions of myeloid cells, thereby minimizing risks associated with ablation of CSF-1R–dependent cells.
35353625.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking the CSF-1 signal with an antibody halted ongoing disease and removed harmful immune cells while sparing essential brain myeloid cells.

35305382.mechanism: Blocks T cell activation and differentiation via ERK
35305382.conclusion_quote: Collectively, spermine alleviates EAE progression by inhibiting CD4 + T cells activation and T effector cell differentiation in a MAPK/ERK-dependent manner, suggesting this pathway might be a target to develop effective therapies for MS.
35305382.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, spermine supplementation reduced disease worsening by calming immune T cells, both when given before and after symptom onset.

35122866.mechanism: Inhibits cathepsin B, reducing Th1, Th17 and Th22 transcription factor signaling
35122866.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that Cathepsin B could be a novel therapeutic candidate against for the treatment of MS.
35122866.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug blocking the enzyme cathepsin B reduced harmful immune cells and improved clinical scores, suggesting cathepsin B as a possible MS treatment target.

35882921.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these results show that antioxidant capacity is relatively conserved between mouse models and MS lesions, and suggest a need to investigate whether the antioxidant elevation in microglia/macrophages is a protective response during oxidative injury, neurodegeneration, and MS.
35882921.summary: Researchers examined antioxidant enzymes in spinal cord lesions of three mouse models of MS and in human MS brain tissue, finding similar patterns.

35076711.conclusion_quote: We suggest that demyelination-related changes in thalamic Ih may be one of the factors defining the prevalence of seizures in MS.
35076711.summary: In C3H/HeJ mice with diet induced demyelination, thalamic pacemaker channel current fell, reducing seizure related brain rhythms and increasing cortical theta activity.

35843522.mechanism: Improves lipid metabolism and reduces inflammatory gene expression
35843522.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, dietary lysolecithin could promote the growth performance, improve hepatic lipid metabolism and regulate inflammation response in juvenile large yellow croaker, and the optimal supplement level of lysolecithin was approximately 0.4% in this study.
35843522.summary: In juvenile large yellow croaker fish, not a multiple sclerosis model, dietary lysolecithin improved growth, lipid metabolism and inflammation related gene expression.

35495042.conclusion_quote: The combined use of VEPs and OCT allowed us to characterize non-invasively, in vivo , the functional and structural changes associated with demyelination and remyelination in a preclinical model of MS.
35495042.summary: In mice fed a cuprizone diet to cause myelin loss, visual evoked potentials detected slowed vision signals that recovered after diet withdrawal, while eye scans showed no nerve thinning.

35076460.mechanism: activates AhR receptor, suppresses IgG1 antibody production
35076460.conclusion_quote: Together these data show that the IgG1 subclass of IgG is a sensitive target of suppression by TCDD.
35076460.summary: In mice with EAE and in laboratory cultures, the environmental pollutant TCDD reduced IgG1 antibody production by B cells and lessened disease.

35328591.mechanism: Hedgehog activation shifts T cells toward Th2 response
35328591.conclusion_quote: These results demonstrate a role for the Hh/ptch pathway in immune response modulation and highlight the usefulness of the ptch +/- mouse model for the study of T-cell-mediated diseases and for the search for new therapeutic strategies in inflammatory diseases.
35328591.summary: In mice with EAE, a genetic change that keeps Hedgehog signalling active caused milder symptoms and less spinal cord damage than normal mice.

34758400.mechanism: Inhibits HDACs, blocks TLR2/MyD88, suppresses M1 microglia
34758400.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these data demonstrate for the first time that belinostat ameliorates EAE in mice through inhibiting neuroinflammation via suppressing M1 microglial polarization, and implicating belinostat as a potential candidate for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
34758400.summary: Belinostat, a drug that blocks histone deacetylase enzymes, reduced symptoms and inflammation in mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, by calming brain immune cells.

35093166.mechanism: Lowers IL-16, which otherwise inhibits myelination
35093166.conclusion_quote: Combined, our data suggests that human hOM-MSCs may have therapeutic benefit in the treatment of MS via an IL-16-mediated pathway, especially if administered during active demyelination and inflammation.
35093166.summary: In mice with EAE, human olfactory mucosa stem cells eased disease even when given late, by lowering IL-16, a protein that blocks myelin repair.

34820577.mechanism: delivers thyroid hormone to oligodendrocyte lineage cells
34820577.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our findings showed that engineered EVPs possess a remarkable CNS lesion targeting potential that offers a potent therapeutic strategy for CNS demyelinating diseases as well as neuroinflammation.
34820577.summary: In mice with EAE, vesicles from engineered neural stem cells carrying thyroid hormone T3 reached damaged myelin areas, slowed disease, protected oligodendrocytes and promoted myelin repair.

36452219.mechanism: Inhibits ROS/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway, promotes M2 microglia polarization
36452219.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these results indicated that FLaAN/C prevents pyroptosis by inhibiting the ROS/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling pathway, and promotes the microglial/macrophage M1/M2 polarization that significantly alleviated inflammation in mouse models of EAE.
36452219.summary: In mice with EAE, a recombinant flagellin protein given after symptom onset reduced inflammation and nerve damage by calming immune cells.

36386488.mechanism: modulates S1P1 receptor, reducing circulating lymphocytes
36386488.summary: In a rat model, newly synthesized triazine-tyrosine compounds designed to target the S1P1 receptor lowered lymphocyte counts, with compounds 5a and 5b most active.

35676325.mechanism: Blocks ferroptosis, an iron-dependent lipid peroxidation cell death
35676325.conclusion_quote: These data indicate that ferroptosis may be a potential target for treating MS.
35676325.summary: Researchers found that blocking ferroptosis, an iron-driven cell death process, improved symptoms and protected nerve cells in mice with EAE.

35600072.conclusion_quote: These data support the notion that reactive astrocytes can inhibit OPC differentiation thereby limiting their remyelination capacity, and that OPCs take on an immune profile in the context of inflammatory cues.
35600072.summary: In human stem cell models from people with MS and healthy controls, inflamed support cells called astrocytes stopped precursor cells from maturing into myelin producing cells.

35077170.mechanism: Activates S1P1 receptor, trapping lymphocytes in lymph nodes
35077170.conclusion_quote: We also confirmed that 21l effectively inhibited lymphocyte egress in the peripheral lymphocyte count test and significantly improved the clinical score in the experimental autoimmune encephalitis MS mouse model.
35077170.summary: In mice with EAE, a newly designed compound called 21l kept immune cells in lymph nodes and significantly improved clinical scores.

34478049.mechanism: Induces autophagy, reducing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in microglia
34478049.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these data suggest that caffeine exerts a newly discovered effect on EAE by reducing NLRP3 inflammasome activation via the induction of autophagy in microglia.
34478049.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, caffeine reduced disease scores, inflammation, and demyelination by boosting autophagy and calming microglia.

35681418.conclusion_quote: In contrast, in the affected neocortical grey matter, the evaluation of anti-IBA1 cell morphologies was the most sensitive method to detect subtle changes of microglial activation.
35681418.summary: In the cuprizone model of demyelination, researchers compared three ways of measuring activated microglia and found that cell shape detected subtle changes best in grey matter.

35073561.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes antibody cross-reactivity between EBV and brain p
