26130320.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, melatonin reduced harmful inflammatory T cells in the blood and brain, increased regulatory T cells, and lessened disease.

26500475.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these data support a model whereby proinflammatory cytokines inhibit SPARCL1 and/or augment SPARC expression by astrocytes in spinal gray matter that, in turn, cause either transient or sustained synaptic retraction from lumbar spinal motor neurons thereby regulating hind limb paralysis during EAE.
26500475.summary: In mice with EAE, paralysis severity tracked with lower SPARCL1 relative to SPARC and fewer synapses on motor neurons, suggesting inflammation drives synapse loss.

26362973.mechanism: promotes intestinal absorption of dietary fats
26362973.conclusion_quote: This study demonstrates that the improvements that can be made with lysolecithin supplementation are highly dependent on the fat incorporated in broiler feeds.
26362973.summary: In broiler chickens, which are not an MS model, adding lysolecithin to feed improved nutrient and fat digestion, with the benefit depending on the type of fat used.

25511803.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes IL-1β and dopamine changes
25511803.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, the present study provides first evidence of the link between the depressive-like behavior and the alteration of dopaminergic system in EAE mice, raising the possibility that IL-1β driven dysfunction of dopaminergic signaling might play a role in mood disturbances also in MS patients.
25511803.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, researchers found depressive-like behavior linked to reduced dopamine release and higher striatal IL-1β, without testing any treatment.

25864804.mechanism: No treatment tested, imaging method only
25864804.conclusion_quote: Thus, we describe a method to analyze and monitor early neuronal damage processes in the brain in vivo.
25864804.summary: In mice with EAE, researchers used a fluorescent calcium sensor and two-photon microscopy to detect early nerve cell and axon damage in living brains during inflammation.

26459920.conclusion_quote: Mononuclear macrophages are therefore, identified as being one of the most significant effector cell types to directly injure the myelin sheath in the CNS.
26459920.summary: In mice with EAE, researchers found that immune cells called macrophages appear to damage the myelin sheath more than cytotoxic T cells do.

25749275.mechanism: Copper chelation alters brain and organ metal levels
25749275.conclusion_quote: These data suggest a possible role of manganese deficiency in the brain in the cuprizone model.
25749275.summary: In mice fed the toxin cuprizone to cause demyelination, copper fell in blood and liver but not brain, while brain manganese was reduced, suggesting manganese loss may contribute.

25724358.mechanism: Not a treatment, describes iron handling protein expression
25724358.conclusion_quote: This data provides the basis for the selective iron accumulation in macrophage/microglia and further evidence of severe mitochondrial dysfunction in EAE.
25724358.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, researchers found iron builds up in spinal cord immune cells called macrophages and microglia, which lack proteins needed to export it.

26531694.conclusion_quote: We conclude that inflammation has a long range effect on the NPCs in the diseased central nervous system, reaching NPC populations outside the lesion sites.
26531694.summary: In EAE, an animal model of MS, neural stem cells far from inflammation made fewer oligodendrocytes and more neurons, showing that inflammation affects distant cells.

26485716.mechanism: Kills dividing immune cells, lowering inflammatory macrophage burden
26485716.conclusion_quote: Overall, 19F MRI can be used to quantitatively monitored EAE disease burden, discover unexpected sites of inflammatory activity, and may serve as a sensitive biomarker for the discovery and preclinical assessment of novel MS therapeutic interventions.
26485716.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of MS, a noninvasive scan measured immune cell buildup, which was reduced by daily treatment with cyclophosphamide.

25347963.mechanism: Not applicable: describes cuprizone-induced brain changes
25347963.conclusion_quote: These results provided neurochemical evidence for the impairment in neuronal functions by cuprizone treatment.
25347963.summary: In young mice fed the toxin cuprizone for six weeks, brain scans showed chemical changes in several regions, along with more anxiety and poorer spatial memory.

26198912.mechanism: reduces autoreactive T cells and proinflammatory cytokines
26198912.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that anti-CD52 therapy may help preserve CNS integrity.
26198912.summary: In mice with EAE, a single course of an antibody against CD52 reduced immune cell infiltration, inflammation, and nerve damage while preserving nerve signaling in the spinal cord.

26722389.mechanism: immunoregulatory cells reduce inflammation, protect axons
26722389.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that Intravenous MSC has the potential to improve the locomotion and regeneration of axons in spinal cord in MOG-induced EAE model.
26722389.summary: In mice with EAE, an MS-like disease, intravenous infusion of mesenchymal stem cells improved walking, preserved healthy spinal cord axons, and lowered inflammation.

26028235.mechanism: No treatment tested, model characterization only
26028235.conclusion_quote: This model can be used as a tool for preclinical studies of the efficiency of multiple sclerosis diagnostic and therapy.
26028235.summary: Researchers fed mice a cuprizone diet to create demyelination, confirming lesions by MRI, reactive astrocytes, and motor and behavioral deficits, as a tool for MS drug testing.

26063423.conclusion_quote: We propose that highly efficient-1 PRF in TMEV provides a mechanism to escape the confines of equimolar expression normally inherent in the single-polyprotein expression strategy of picornaviruses.
26063423.summary: This virology study found that Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus uses a highly efficient ribosomal frameshift to make its proteins, with no MS treatment tested.

27600243.conclusion_quote: Importantly, this technology allows simultaneous detection of serum antibody activities among the three major classes of antigens, i.e., lipids, carbohydrates, and proteins.
27600243.summary: Researchers built a chip printed with liposomes, proteins and sugars that detects antibodies to all three antigen types, and used it to track autoantibody changes in mice with EAE.

25536292.mechanism: Measures how DNA aptamers distribute through mouse tissues
25536292.conclusion_quote: Modeling of tissue distribution data reveals the importance of DNA aptamer sequence, 3' modification, and protein conjugation in enhancing tissue exposure.
25536292.summary: In healthy mice, this study measured how DNA aptamers and their streptavidin conjugates spread to tissues including the brain after injection, without testing disease effects.

25512344.mechanism: blocks CysLT1 receptor, reducing Th17 cell recruitment to CNS
25512344.conclusion_quote: Thus, leukotrienes may act as chemoattractants for Th17 cells.
25512344.summary: In an animal model of EAE, the drug montelukast blocked leukotriene signals, which eased symptoms and reduced Th17 immune cells entering the central nervous system.

26067430.conclusion_quote: These results highlight the relevance of the cuprizone model to study MS-related gray matter pathology and neurodegeneration.
26067430.summary: In a mouse model of MS, five weeks of cuprizone diet caused widespread gray matter demyelination, while most white matter tracts stayed intact.

24810631.mechanism: activates endogenous protein C to generate APC
24810631.conclusion_quote: These data suggest that symptomatic MS may respond to a treatment strategy that involves temporal pharmacological enhancement of endogenous APC generation.
24810631.summary: In mice with EAE, a thrombin analog that boosts the body's own protein C reduced disease severity, inflammation, and myelin loss when given after symptoms began.

25449910.conclusion_quote: Blocking both apoptosis and necroptosis restored virus yields.
25449910.summary: In cultured macrophages from mice infected with Theiler's virus, a model of MS-like demyelination, blocking cell death pathways restored virus yields. The study mainly describes how infected cells die.

25589073.mechanism: blocks CD28 costimulation of T cells
25589073.conclusion_quote: Blocking rhesus monkey CD28 with FR104 mitigated autoreactive T and B cell activation and prevented CNS pathology in the rhMOG/CFA EAE model in rhesus monkeys.
25589073.summary: In rhesus monkeys with EAE, an antibody fragment blocking the CD28 immune signal prevented disease, reduced brain inflammation, and protected myelin from damage.

26036872.mechanism: suppresses T-cell proliferation and pro-inflammatory cytokines
26036872.conclusion_quote: The therapeutic effect of hAECs is in part mediated by inducing an anti-inflammatory response within the CNS, demonstrating that hAECs hold promise for the treatment of autoimmune diseases like MS.
26036872.summary: In mice with a relapsing MS-like disease (EAE), human amnion epithelial cells reduced inflammation, prevented relapses, and increased calming immune cells.

26671084.conclusion_quote: These data indicate that BCD in humans might worsen CNS viral infections and might not improve disability accrual in MS.
26671084.summary: In mice infected with a virus that causes demyelinating disease, depleting B cells with an anti-CD20 antibody worsened brain infection and disability without improving long-term outcomes.

25052203.mechanism: Stimulates AT2 receptor, reducing T-cell and microglia activation
25052203.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that AT2R stimulation protects the myelin sheaths in autoimmune central nervous system inflammation by inhibiting the T-cell response and microglia activation.
25052203.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug stimulating the angiotensin type 2 receptor reduced immune cell activation and myelin loss and improved neurological scores.

25393803.mechanism: Intranasal tolerogenic MOG fusion shifts immune response to regulatory
25393803.conclusion_quote: Thus, despite a detectable effect on relevant immune parameters, the fusion protein failed to influence the clinical and pathological outcome of disease.
25393803.summary: In mice and marmosets with EAE, an intranasal tolerizing MOG fusion protein changed immune markers but did not improve disease course or pathology.

26198937.conclusion_quote: We found that fingolimod did not have any effect on cerebellar remyelination, number of mature oligodendrocytes, microglia or astrocytes when fed after cuprizone exposure.
26198937.summary: In the cuprizone model of myelin damage, fingolimod given after the damage did not improve cerebellar myelin repair or change nearby support cell numbers.

25326791.conclusion_quote: Additionally, reactive astrocytes abundantly present in the lumbar spinal cord parenchyma were identified as principal cell type with significantly elevated eN expression.
25326791.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of MS, ecto-5'-nucleotidase rose during symptoms, mainly in reactive astrocytes, and a second protein form appeared.

25725102.mechanism: Loss of CXCL10 reduces early microglial activation
25725102.conclusion_quote: Our results show that CXCL10 actively participates in the initiation of microglial activation.
25725102.summary: In mice given cuprizone, a toxin that damages myelin, removing the CXCL10 gene reduced early microglial activation and later nerve damage.

25777301.mechanism: deficiency reduces granzyme B in memory T cells
25777301.conclusion_quote: Taken together, IRF3 plays an important role in the maintenance of effective anti-viral T cell memory responses.
25777301.summary: In knockout mice lacking IRF3, Theiler's virus persisted and memory T cells made less granzyme B, showing IRF3 supports lasting antiviral T cell responses.

25810515.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes T-cell behaviour in CNS
25810515.conclusion_quote: Therefore, intravital imaging demonstrates that local myelin recognition by autoreactive CD8(+) T cells in inflammatory CNS lesions alone is not sufficient to induce disability or increase axonal injury.
25810515.summary: In a mouse model of MS, researchers watched CD8 T cells that recognise myelin enter inflamed spinal lesions, finding they did not cause disability or extra axon damage.

25410153.mechanism: Suppresses myelin-specific T cell proliferation and inflammation
25410153.conclusion_quote: Mice injected with Acthar to treat the second attack had a significantly lower mean clinical score during relapse and a significantly reduced cumulative disease burden compared to Placebo gel-treated mice.
25410153.summary: In mice with relapsing MS-like disease, Acthar gel given during a second flare reduced symptom scores and spinal cord inflammation compared with placebo gel.

25721871.mechanism: activates Nrf2 antioxidant response and suppresses IL-17A
25721871.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our data suggest that DMF treatment in the effector phase may suppress TMEV-IDD not only via enhancing the antioxidant response but also via suppressing IL-17A.
25721871.summary: In mice with Theiler's virus-induced demyelinating disease, dimethyl fumarate given during the effector phase reduced clinical and spinal cord damage by boosting antioxidant defenses and lowering IL-17A.

25595260.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes disease biology
25595260.conclusion_quote: These findings support the idea that the meninges are a gateway for immune cell access into the CNS, a finding that has important therapeutic implications.
25595260.summary: In mice with relapsing EAE, inflammation in the meninges, the membranes around the brain and spinal cord, tracks with flare ups, and T cells enter these membranes during relapses.

26253956.conclusion_quote: Our findings indicate that enhancing remyelination may be a potential therapy for schizophrenia.
26253956.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, the drug clemastine boosted myelin repair and reversed schizophrenia-like behavior changes.

25468271.mechanism: Not applicable, describes donor memory cell persistence
25468271.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest the early onset of disease seen in recipients recovered from adoptively transferred disease and challenged with encephalitogen is due to the sustained presence of donor-derived memory cells.
25468271.summary: In mice with EAE, donor immune memory cells persisted after recovery and explained why recovered animals got sick earlier when exposed again to the trigger.

26092157.mechanism: Not applicable, no treatment or genetic change tested
26092157.conclusion_quote: We conclude that EAE at this early stage does not significantly affect CNS cellular respiration and this might underlie the reason for the recovery of diseased rats.
26092157.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of MS, researchers found that spinal cord energy production did not change during early disease, though mitochondria were smaller in susceptible rats.

25282335.mechanism: Antibodies neutralize IL-17, reducing Th17-driven inflammation in optic nerve
25282335.conclusion_quote: Thus, the optic nerve compartment is particularly prone to support IL-17 mediated inflammatory responses during CNS autoimmunity and structural integrity of the retina can be preserved by neutralizing IL-17.
25282335.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking IL-17 with antibodies did not fully stop paralysis but completely prevented thinning of the retinal nerve layers in the eye.

26060310.mechanism: Removing DBC1 prevents FOXP3 degradation during inflammation
26060310.conclusion_quote: These findings establish a previously unidentified mechanism regulating FOXP3 stability during inflammation and reveal a pathway for potential therapeutic modulation and intervention in inflammatory diseases.
26060310.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, removing the DBC1 gene made regulatory T cells more resistant to inflammation, delaying and lessening disease.

26193120.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrate that a pain-mediated neural signal can be transformed into an inflammation reaction at specific vessels to induce disease relapse, thus making this signal a potential therapeutic target.
26193120.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, pain triggered a nerve signal that drew immune cells into the spinal cord and caused relapse.

26322802.conclusion_quote: The online version of the article has been corrected to reflect this change.
26322802.summary: This correction notice concerns a study of EAE in adult offspring of mothers with gestational hypothyroidism and adds a missing funding source.

26439961.mechanism: No treatment tested, age-related barrier disruption described
26439961.conclusion_quote: We suggest strong correlations between NADPH oxidase and the other factors play important roles in increased BBB disruption and EAE susceptibility in middle-aged mice.
26439961.summary: In mice with EAE, six-month-old mice had more severe disease and leakier blood brain barriers than six-week-old mice, with inflammatory markers rising together.

25630465.mechanism: Deleting NFAT1 or NFAT2 changes T-cell cytokine production
25630465.conclusion_quote: Here, we demonstrate an essential role for NFAT in disease induction, as the combined lack of NFAT1 (NFATc2) and NFAT2 (NFATc1) completely protected mice.
25630465.summary: Mice lacking the NFAT1 or NFAT2 immune transcription factors had milder EAE, a mouse model of multiple sclerosis, and lacking both fully protected them from disease.

25778803.mechanism: Blocks RIPK2 kinase, reducing inflammatory cytokine production
25778803.conclusion_quote: Our study highlights the importance of the kinase activity of RIPK2 for proper immune responses and demonstrates the therapeutic potential of inhibiting RIPK2 in NOD-driven inflammatory diseases.
25778803.summary: In mice with EAE, a RIPK2 kinase inhibitor called WEHI-345 prevented inflammatory cytokine production and improved the disease.

25944279.conclusion_quote: Collectively, the results showed cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the target organ specific sexual dimorphism in the T lymphocyte-dependent immune/inflammatory response, and suggested a substantial role for the target organ in shaping the sexually dimorphic clinical outcome of EAE.
25944279.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of MS, males had more severe disease than females, with more inflammatory immune cells in the spinal cord.

26216045.mechanism: blocks dectin-1 receptor during disease induction
26216045.conclusion_quote: Thus dectin-1 plays a critical role in the ability of complete Freund's adjuvant to induce EAU in mice.
26216045.summary: In mice with experimental autoimmune uveoretinitis, an eye inflammation model, blocking the dectin-1 receptor during induction prevented disease development.

25704809.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes MMP-2/9 chemokine leukocyte migration
25704809.conclusion_quote: Hence, cytokines, chemokines, and cytokine-induced MMP-2/9 activity specifically at the inflammatory border collectively act to accelerate leukocyte chemotaxis across the parenchymal border.
25704809.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, researchers found that chemokines and MMP-2 and MMP-9 enzymes at the brain barrier together speed immune cells into the nervous system.

25586993.mechanism: Reduced BDNF limits oligodendrocyte progenitor proliferation after demyelination
25586993.conclusion_quote: Therefore, levels of BDNF influence the proliferation of OPCs resulting from a demyelinating lesion.
25586993.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, having less BDNF blunted the increase in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells by reducing how many of them divided.

25595256.mechanism: Not a treatment study, measures LIF secretion
25595256.conclusion_quote: This is a heretofore unreported aspect of immune dysregulation in patients with RR-MS that may be related to insufficient remyelination and neurogenesis in MS lesions.
25595256.summary: In human immune cells from people with relapsing MS, stimulated cells released less leukemia inhibitory factor than healthy controls, suggesting immune dysregulation.

25819415.mechanism: Inhibits oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation into mature oligodendrocytes
25819415.conclusion_quote: Together, these data suggest that IGFBP-7 was up regulated during EAE and inhibit the transition from OPCs to mature OLs, implying its use as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of inflammatory demyelinating diseases.
25819415.summary: In mice with EAE, the protein IGFBP-7 rose in the spinal cord and was found to slow immature cells from maturing into myelin-producing cells.

26425145.conclusion_quote: Safe and effective methods of inducing long-lasting immune tolerance are essential for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
26425145.summary: This review describes how the immune system can be trained to tolerate myelin attacks, but it tests no new treatment in animals or people.

26077720.mechanism: Gene loss favors regulatory T cell generation
26077720.conclusion_quote: This study provides evidence that a bioactive lipid, LysoPS, negatively influences T reg cell accumulation and activity through GPR174.
26077720.summary: In mice lacking the GPR174 gene, regulatory T immune cells formed more readily and mice had milder experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, a model of MS.

26115190.conclusion_quote: Our data indicate that oligodendroglial regeneration and remyelination are enhanced in the maturing rodent brain compared with the young-adult rodent brain.
26115190.summary: In young and adult mice given the toxin cuprizone, which damages myelin, juvenile mice lost myelin faster but repaired it sooner than adults.

26341401.mechanism: Blocks GM-CSF signaling in inflammatory monocytes
26341401.conclusion_quote: These results indicate that GM-CSF signaling controls a pathogenic expression signature in CCR2(+)Ly6C(hi) monocytes and their progeny, which was essential for tissue damage.
26341401.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the GM-CSF receptor from CCR2 positive inflammatory monocytes prevented disease, showing these cells drive tissue damage.

25585346.mechanism: Not applicable: describes disease mechanism only
25585346.conclusion_quote: However, these changes were unable to modify the intensity of response, which explains the chronic progression of the disease in both concentrations.
25585346.summary: In mice with EAE, two different doses of the MOG immunizing peptide triggered different inflammation patterns and regulatory responses but the same chronic disease course.

interventions: local blockades of these growth factors
25556244.mechanism: blocks growth factors, reducing chemokine and IL-6 expression
25556244.conclusion_quote: The results suggest that the temporal expression of growth factors is involved in the inflammation development seen in several diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis and MS.
25556244.summary: In mice with arthritis and an MS model called EAE, blocking growth factors such as epiregulin reduced inflammation, and these growth factors were also raised in people with MS.

25595261.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes age-related immune changes
25595261.conclusion_quote: Thus, the study suggests that age-associated changes leading to entrapping of activated CD4+ cells in the spleen could contribute to the restriction in development of EAE in aged rats.
25595261.summary: In aged rats with EAE, a model of MS, immune cells became trapped in the spleen and fewer rats developed disease than in young rats.

26566674.mechanism: Deleting sortilin gene in mice or immune cells
26566674.conclusion_quote: Considering our results and recent data from other investigators, we conclude that the proneurotrophin receptor sortilin plays a role in innate, rather than in adaptive, immune processes and, thus, not in autoimmune neuroinflammation.
26566674.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the sortilin gene did not change how susceptible the animals were to autoimmune brain inflammation, suggesting sortilin is not a key driver.

26494278.mechanism: Not applicable, no MS treatment tested
26494278.conclusion_quote: These results question the widely held view that the BBB is largely disrupted in AD, raising concern about assumptions of drug permeability in disease.
26494278.summary: In mice and human brain tissue from Alzheimer's studies, the blood-brain barrier stayed largely intact, challenging assumptions about how well drugs enter the brain.

25641089.mechanism: blocks immune cell entry into the nervous system
25641089.conclusion_quote: Results indicate that natalizumab may also be beneficial in MS with B cell-driven immunopathogenesis.
25641089.summary: In mice with an MS model driven by both T and B cells, an antibody like natalizumab improved disease and reduced spinal cord damage when given early, but not late.

25533628.mechanism: Blocks CD30 ligand, reducing Th1 and Th17 cells
25533628.conclusion_quote: These results indicate that CD30L/CD30 signaling is critically involved in antigen-specific CD4 T cell responses at both the induction and effector phase, thus could be a new target molecule for the treatment of central nervous system autoimmunity.
25533628.summary: In mice with EAE, a soluble CD30 fusion protein that blocks CD30 ligand reduced clinical symptoms whether given before or after disease onset, by limiting Th1 and Th17 immune cells.

26587553.mechanism: Blocks LPS-induced myeloid activation and TNF-alpha secretion
26587553.conclusion_quote: The inhibition of myeloid cell activation may be part of the immunosuppressive action of fingolimod and take place in the periphery and in the CNS.
26587553.summary: In mice with EAE, fingolimod reduced inflammatory TNF-alpha production by immune cells in the spleen and brain, and it also dampened activation of human monocytes in the lab.

26511769.conclusion_quote: Thus, our data identify a unique cell surface signature, trafficking mechanism and T-cell intrinsic regulators of GM-CSF/IFNγ-producing Th17 cells.
26511769.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, researchers found that inflammatory immune cells can be identified by a receptor switch from CCR6 to CCR2 during their development.

25499467.mechanism: TGF-β isoforms limit differentiation of encephalitogenic Th17 cells
25499467.conclusion_quote: Thus, TGF-β, irrespective of isoform, negatively regulates the differentiation of encephalitogenic Th17 cells.
25499467.summary: In mice with EAE, T cells grown with TGF-β1 or TGF-β3 made lots of IL-17 but did not cause disease, showing both forms block development of disease-causing Th17 cells.

25741342.mechanism: removes T-bet from regulatory T cells
25741342.conclusion_quote: These observations demonstrate that, although Treg can acquire characteristics associated with pathogenic T effector cells, this process is not necessarily required for their suppressive capacity and the resolution of autoimmune inflammation.
25741342.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, removing T-bet from regulatory T cells did not change their recruitment to the brain and spinal cord or how well the disease resolved.

26141421.mechanism: Describes chemokine expression, no treatment tested
26141421.conclusion_quote: These data, the first study of cytokines in central nervous system tissue and cerebrospinal fluid in TMEV-IDD, support the hypothesis that multiple sclerosis is caused by chronic infection with an as-yet unidentified pathogen, possibly a picornavirus.
26141421.summary: In mice infected with Theiler's virus, a model of MS, chemokines CXCL10, CXCL9 and CCL5 rose in spinal cord and spinal fluid, matching human MS.

26408399.conclusion_quote: Together, these results point to (i) an age-specificity in CD4+ cell-mediated immune response and (ii) mechanisms underlying the sex differences in this response in aged rats.
26408399.summary: In aged rats with EAE, a model of MS, males developed milder disease than females, with fewer activated CD4+ T cells and less inflammation in the spinal cord.

26137596.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest altered blood B-cell homeostasis in MS patients.
26137596.summary: Researchers measured B cell types in blood from 32 people with multiple sclerosis and 34 healthy people, finding more CD19 positive B cells in patients but normal regulatory B cells.

26216117.conclusion_quote: It is concluded that LIF may have an important role in the process of remyelination by increasing Opalin expression and MOG expression.
26216117.summary: In mice with cuprizone induced demyelination, injected leukemia inhibitory factor increased Opalin and MOG myelin proteins in the cerebral cortex, suggesting a role in remyelination.

25948818.mechanism: induces myelin-specific Tregs that block dendritic cell migration
25948818.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our data demonstrate a novel model for deciphering the Ag-specific Foxp3(+) Treg-mediated mechanisms of tolerance and delineate iDCs as a Foxp3(+) Treg cellular target in unmanipulated mice.
25948818.summary: In mice with EAE, infusing myelin induced myelin-specific regulatory T cells that reduced harmful dendritic cells reaching lymph nodes and eased disease.

25888258.mechanism: NLRP12 normally restrains T-cell IL-4 production
25888258.conclusion_quote: These results define an unexpected role for NLRP12 as an intrinsic negative regulator of T-cell-mediated immunity and identify altered NF-κB regulation and IL-4 production as key mediators of NLRP12-associated disease.
25888258.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the NLRP12 gene made T cells more inflamed and caused unusual balance and coordination problems through increased IL-4 production.

25432322.mechanism: Not applicable, describes protein expression only
25432322.conclusion_quote: Overall, these findings suggest that both isoforms of Dab-2 are transiently upregulated in response to SCI and that the increased expression of Dab-2 is associated with the early activation of macrophages and astrogliosis in the course of CNS inflammation.
25432322.summary: In rats with spinal cord injury, the protein Disabled 2 temporarily increased in immune and support cells. No treatment was tested.

25689841.mechanism: NFATc1 loss reduces Th17 and IFN-γ responses
25689841.conclusion_quote: Altogether, these results reveal an important role of NFATc1 in inducing Th17-cell responses and IFN-γ, both being relevant for the EAE development.
25689841.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting NFATc1 in T cells reduced disease severity, brain and spinal cord inflammation, and harmful immune signals.

26538779.mechanism: Stimulates myelin production and oligodendrocyte progenitor increase
26538779.conclusion_quote: Overall, our results indicate that progesterone treatment can stimulate myelin production and that it may provide a feasible and practical way for remyelination in diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
26538779.summary: In mice given cuprizone to strip myelin, progesterone implants started after the diet stopped increased remyelination and myelin protein levels compared with placebo.

26100487.mechanism: Induces IL-10 that suppresses autoaggressive T cells, limiting CNS migration
26100487.conclusion_quote: Our findings demonstrate that a bacterial infection of the respiratory tract can attenuate EAE by promoting production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 that may suppress licensing of autoaggressive T cells in the lungs, thereby preventing their migration into the CNS.
26100487.summary: In mice with EAE, a respiratory infection with Bordetella pertussis reduced disease severity and brain and spinal cord inflammation by increasing IL-10, a protein that calms immune responses.

26600308.mechanism: Not applicable, observational clinical study of patient blood
26600308.conclusion_quote: To our knowledge, this is the first report demonstrating that higher blood BAFF levels may reflect a more stable and effective MS treatment outcome.
26600308.summary: Over 2.3 years, researchers measured the blood protein BAFF in 170 people with relapsing MS, finding higher levels linked to stable disease and better treatment response.

26477780.mechanism: Not applicable, describes disease mechanism only
26477780.conclusion_quote: These observations are consistent with previous measurements of excitatory currents suggesting different mechanisms of seizure generation during the acute infection and during chronic epilepsy.
26477780.summary: In mice infected with Theiler's virus, a model of virus-induced epilepsy, inhibitory signals in brain cells of the CA3 region dropped during acute infection and recovered two months later.

25680271.mechanism: Ezh2 maintains regulatory T cell identity during activation
25680271.conclusion_quote: These studies reveal a critical role for Ezh2 in the maintenance of Treg cell identity during cellular activation.
25680271.summary: Mice lacking Ezh2 in regulatory T cells developed spontaneous autoimmunity and had impaired recovery from EAE, a model of MS.

25639498.conclusion_quote: Our results confirm that pool size ratio measurements correlate with myelin content, with the correlation coefficient depending on strain and staining method, and demonstrate the in vivo applicability of this MRI technique to experimental mouse models of multiple sclerosis.
25639498.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause myelin loss and recovery, an MRI measure of myelin correlated with tissue staining, supporting its use in living mouse models of MS.

25917331.mechanism: Increases blood brain barrier permeability and CNS pathology in a sex specific w
25917331.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrate that the effects of dietary sodium on autoimmune neuroinflammation are sex specific, genetically controlled, and CNS mediated.
25917331.summary: In mice with EAE, a high salt diet worsened disease in both sexes in one strain and only in females in another, depending on genetics and sex.

25794633.mechanism: activates TLR4 receptor, promoting Th17 cell differentiation
25794633.conclusion_quote: These findings provide the first evidence that TLR4 activation directly regulate Th17 differentiation.
25794633.summary: In mouse T cells and mice with EAE, the bacterial molecule LPS boosted development of inflammatory Th17 immune cells and made the disease worse.

26371185.mechanism: removes CTLA4 from regulatory T cells
26371185.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our findings point to a profound role for CTLA-4 on T reg cells in limiting their peripheral expansion and activation, thereby regulating the phenotype and function of T conv cells.
26371185.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the CTLA4 gene from adult regulatory T cells protected against disease without causing systemic autoimmunity.

26362814.conclusion_quote: Our results support the model that the medial habenula responds to disease activity by upregulating transferrin receptor to facilitate the movement of iron into the brain from the third ventricle, raising the possibility that a similar mechanism accounts for iron accumulation in deep gray matter structures in patients with multiple sclerosis.
26362814.summary: In mice with cerebral EAE, a mouse model of MS, the medial habenula showed more transferrin receptor and iron, hinting at how iron builds up in MS.

26844268.mechanism: Myelin lipid breakdown supplies ketone fuel in aging
26844268.conclusion_quote: This mechanistic pathway and its chronologically phased activation, links mitochondrial dysfunction early in aging with later age development of white matter degeneration.
26844268.summary: In an animal model of aging female brains, breakdown of myelin fats supplies ketone fuel alongside mitochondrial decline and white matter degeneration.

26213925.mechanism: Gene deletion, compensation by other potassium channels
26213925.conclusion_quote: In an experimental model of autoimmune neuroinflammation, K2P5.1-/- mice show a comparable disease course to wild-type animals and no major changes in the peripheral immune system or CNS compartment.
26213925.summary: In mice lacking the K2P5.1 potassium channel gene, the autoimmune model of MS (EAE) progressed the same as in normal mice, because other channels compensated.

25437876.mechanism: Blocks PDHK1, shifting T cells away from glycolysis
25437876.conclusion_quote: Together, these data show that CD4+ subsets utilize and require distinct metabolic programs that can be targeted to control specific T cell populations in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.
25437876.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking the PDHK1 enzyme reduced harmful Th17 immune cells and increased protective Treg cells, which eased the disease.

25415436.mechanism: limits effector T cell survival and expansion
25415436.conclusion_quote: Together, our data suggest that PDPN functions as an inhibitory molecule on T cells, thereby promoting tissue tolerance by limiting long-term survival and maintenance of CD4+ effector T cells in target organs.
25415436.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the Pdpn gene worsened disease, while overexpressing it on T cells speeded recovery by reducing CD4 T cells in the brain and spinal cord.

25448765.mechanism: Describes blood-brain barrier breakdown before lesion formation
25448765.conclusion_quote: Our findings suggest that BBB breach occurs before significant immune cell infiltration and demyelination.
25448765.summary: In mice with spontaneous relapsing EAE and in MS patient lesions, the blood brain barrier leaked before immune cells invaded and myelin was lost.

25456971.mechanism: Blocks oxysterol making, reducing T cell CNS migration
25456971.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our results support a pro-inflammatory role for oxysterols during EAE and identify oxysterols as a potential therapeutic target to treat autoimmune diseases.
25456971.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the Ch25h gene reduced oxysterol production, limited harmful T cells reaching the brain and spinal cord, and eased disease course.

26374165.conclusion_quote: The dissection of signalling pathways regulating Del-1 expression provides potential targets to treat inflammatory diseases associated with diminished Del-1 expression, such as periodontitis and multiple sclerosis.
26374165.summary: Human endothelial cells and mice with gum inflammation showed that IL-17 reduces the protective protein Del-1, and D-resolvins can reverse this effect.

25744944.mechanism: Not applicable: review of environmental factors
25744944.conclusion_quote: A better knowledge of the influence of various environmental stimuli on MS risk and course would certainly allow the development of add-on therapies or measures in parallel to the immunotherapies currently used in MS.
25744944.summary: This review article summarizes how viruses, vitamin D, sunlight, and gut microbes may influence multiple sclerosis risk, mostly in childhood.

26481340.mechanism: Inhibits Rho kinase, preserving neurite growth and synapses
26481340.conclusion_quote: Fasudil could promote synaptogenesis and thus may contribute to preventing irreversible neurological disability associated with MS.
26481340.summary: In mice with EAE and in mouse neurons exposed to serum from MS patients, the drug Fasudil blocked Rho kinase and helped neurons grow and form synapses.

26416183.mechanism: induces autophagy and cell death in autoreactive T cells
26416183.conclusion_quote: Taken together, the data provide new insights into the role of DHT and indicate that cell death and autophagy contribute to the therapeutic effects of androgens in autoreactive T cells.
26416183.summary: In laboratory tests on autoreactive T cells from mice with EAE, dihydrotestosterone killed these cells and triggered autophagy, and reduced their cytokine production.

26884844.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that AQP4 and selective cytokines in serum are associated with ION pathogenesis in the animal model, and these results shine light for future clinical diagnosis as potential biomarkers in ION patients.
26884844.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of inflammatory nerve damage, researchers measured AQP4 and immune signaling molecules in optic nerves and blood, suggesting possible biomarkers for optic neuritis.

25691003.mechanism: Astrocyte IL-10 reshapes microglia and boosts lymphocyte entry
25691003.conclusion_quote: Altogether, our findings suggested that astrocyte-targeted production of IL-10 impacted the microglial response and lymphocyte recruitment and culminated in a beneficial effect on neuronal survival.
25691003.summary: In transgenic mice producing extra IL-10 in astrocytes, facial nerve injury caused fewer dying motor neurons, with changed microglia and more lymphocytes.

25637488.mechanism: reduces inflammation, demyelination and axonal damage
25637488.conclusion_quote: However, there is an antagonistic interaction between CBD and PEA in protection against MOG-induced disease.
25637488.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, cannabidiol and palmitoylethanolamide each eased symptoms and damage, but giving them together worked less well than either alone.

26618510.mechanism: Activates NRF2 antioxidant pathway and reduces inflammation
26618510.conclusion_quote: We conclude that immunomodulatory and neuroprotective dimethyl fumarate may represent an innovative therapeutic option in human autoimmune neuropathies.
26618510.summary: In Lewis rats with experimental autoimmune neuritis, a model of nerve inflammation, dimethyl fumarate given before disease onset reduced nerve inflammation, demyelination and axonal damage.

25576296.mechanism: Lowers BACE-1 and raises BDNF to protect axons
25576296.conclusion_quote: We conclude that this novel natural reagent, MAT, which effectively protects neuro-axons from CNS inflammation-induced damage, could be a potential candidate for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases such as MS.
25576296.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of MS, matrine reduced clinical disease, inflammation, myelin loss and axonal damage while increasing brain-derived neurotrophic factor in the CNS.

25755209.mechanism: Anti-seizure drugs reduce seizures and affect brain cell responses
25755209.conclusion_quote: The TMEV model thus provides an etiologically relevant platform to evaluate potential treatments for acute seizures and disease modification.
25755209.summary: In mice infected with a virus that can cause seizures, valproic acid reduced seizures and improved motor performance, while carbamazepine increased seizures and anxiety-like behavior.

25727069.mechanism: blocks B7 binding to CD28 costimulation
25727069.conclusion_quote: Taken together, B7 blockade at a particular stage of the autoimmune response can result in the suppression of Treg cells, leading to a more severe disease.
25727069.summary: In mice with EAE, an MS model, blocking B7 signals with CTLA-4Ig early in disease worsened inflammation, demyelination and symptoms by suppressing regulatory T cells.

26744883.mechanism: Blocks Fas, caspase-3 and Bax/Bcl-2 apoptosis pathways
26744883.conclusion_quote: We have demonstrated that, alone, purified CBD possesses an anti-apoptotic power against the neurodegenerative processes underlying MS development.
26744883.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, injected purified cannabidiol reduced signals of nerve cell death in the spinal cord.

26062998.mechanism: Loss of Eos reduces conventional T-cell activation and IL-17
26062998.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our studies are not consistent with a role for Eos in Treg development and function but demonstrate that Eos plays an important role in the activation and differentiation of Tconvs.
26062998.summary: In mice lacking Eos, regulatory T cells worked normally, but conventional T cells made less IL-2, and experimental MS (EAE) was more severe.

25776919.conclusion_quote: Also, by using an antibody-mediated IL-23 depletion model, we further demonstrate that optimal fungal clearance, but not survival, depends on an intact Th17 response.
25776919.summary: In mice infected with a fungus causing sporotrichosis, an intact Th17 immune response was needed to clear the infection, though not to survive it. This study does not involve multiple sclerosis.

25976303.mechanism: activates PKA and PKC signaling via TLR4, boosting survival and growth genes
25976303.conclusion_quote: Thus, we propose that sPIF imparts neuroprotection via multiple mechanisms at multiple levels downstream of TLR4.
25976303.summary: In a rat newborn brain injury model, a synthetic peptide called sPIF reduced cell death and restored brain structure by activating PKA and PKC signaling, not an MS model.

25844901.mechanism: Lacking 12/15-LO enzyme speeds dendritic cell maturation
25844901.conclusion_quote: Together, our data reveal that 12/15-LO controls maturation of DCs and implicate enzymatic lipid oxidation in shaping the adaptive immune response.
25844901.summary: In mice lacking the 12/15-LO enzyme, immune dendritic cells matured faster and drove more Th17 cells, making experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis worse.

26732345.mechanism: Reduces microglial activation by normalizing STIM1-mediated calcium entry
26732345.conclusion_quote: Overall, our data suggested that Que may inhibit microglial activation by neutralization of the LPS-induced abnormal STIM1-mediated intercellular calcium homeostasis.
26732345.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, the antipsychotic quetiapine reduced harmful microglia activity in the brain and promoted myelin repair.

25388635.mechanism: Anti-inflammatory, lowers nitric oxide and inflammatory cells
25388635.conclusion_quote: These data indicate that G2013 therapy can attenuate the disease progression in experimental model of MS.
25388635.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the experimental drug G2013 lowered disease rates, reduced severity and inflammation, and delayed onset.

26385521.conclusion_quote: These findings indicate that thymic-derived Treg affinity range matches that of their Tconvs in the periphery and suggest a change in TCR affinity as a potential mechanism for autoimmune progression and escape from immune regulation.
26385521.summary: In mice with EAE, regulatory and effector T cells that target myelin had similar binding strength in lymph nodes, while effector cells in the CNS bound more strongly.

25893602.mechanism: Loss of TREM2 impairs microglial myelin debris clearance
25893602.conclusion_quote: We conclude that TREM2 is required for promoting microglial expansion during aging and microglial response to insults of the white matter.
25893602.summary: In mice lacking Trem2, microglia failed to clear myelin debris after cuprizone-induced demyelination, leading to persistent white matter damage and oligodendrocyte loss.

25703787.conclusion_quote: IL-16 selectively regulates migration of all CD4 expressing T cells regardless of their activation state, which is of critical importance for immune modulation and potential therapy of MS.
25703787.summary: This review explains how the cytokine IL-16 may regulate immune cells involved in multiple sclerosis and could guide future treatments.

26338327.mechanism: Inactivates PTPRZ receptor, promoting oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation
26338327.conclusion_quote: Therefore, PTPRZ inactivation in OPCs by PTN, which is secreted from demyelinated axons, may be the mechanism responsible for oligodendrocyte differentiation during reparative remyelination in the CNS.
26338327.summary: In cuprizone-treated mice, removing the Ptprz gene sped up remyelination, and the signaling molecule pleiotrophin helped precursor cells mature into myelin-making cells.

25681574.mechanism: Blocks LINGO-1 signaling, enhancing remyelination and axon repair
25681574.conclusion_quote: These data provide morphometric and functional evidence of enhancement of remyelination associated with antagonism of LINGO-1.
25681574.summary: In mice with spinal cord demyelination, blocking LINGO-1 through gene knockout or an antibody improved nerve signal recovery and increased remyelination.

26669675.mechanism: Deleting apoE gene alters immune response in EAE
26669675.conclusion_quote: apoE exerts moderate sex-specific effects on EAE severity.
26669675.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the apoE gene had sex based effects: males improved slightly while females worsened.

25533291.conclusion_quote: Puberty in females enhances CNS autoimmune mechanisms that lead to MS in humans and EAE in mice.
25533291.summary: In girls, later menarche was linked to lower MS risk, and pubertal female mice with EAE were more susceptible than prepubertal ones.

26110560.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our results underline that APC and NogoA are reliable markers for detection of mature oligodendrocytes.
26110560.summary: Researchers studied mice fed the cuprizone diet to test markers that identify oligodendrocytes, finding APC and NogoA reliably mark mature cells.

25499583.mechanism: blocks acid-sensing ion channels during acidosis
25499583.conclusion_quote: Therefore pharmacological modulation of ASICs in neuroinflammatory diseases could represent a new promising strategy for future therapies aimed at neuro-protection.
25499583.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug that blocks acid sensing ion channels protected neuron activity and presynaptic terminals, eased symptoms, and reduced nerve damage.

25189319.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes disease marker behavior
25189319.conclusion_quote: These important findings underpin the reliability of NAA quantification as a valid marker for the paraclinical determination of the extent of neurodegeneration, even under conditions of oligodendrocyte loss in which impaired metabolization of NAA is expected.
25189319.summary: Using the cuprizone model of demyelination, brain NAA levels did not rise despite oligodendrocyte loss, supporting NAA scans as a reliable measure of nerve damage.

26017142.mechanism: Inhibits NADPH oxidase assembly, reducing reactive oxygen species production
26017142.conclusion_quote: These results demonstrate that apocynin inhibits the clinical features and neuropathological changes associated with EAE.
26017142.summary: Apocynin, a drug that blocks an enzyme producing harmful oxidants, reduced paralysis, demyelination and immune cell infiltration in mice with EAE, even when given after symptoms began.

26179268.conclusion_quote: Several mechanisms cooperate to alter immunogenicity.
26179268.summary: This review explains how pairs of complementary proteins can become more immune-provoking, drawing on past studies in several animal models of autoimmune disease, not on new experiments.

25869475.mechanism: blocks CD8 T-cell entry across blood-brain barrier
25869475.conclusion_quote: Our data demonstrate that MCAM identifies encephalitogenic CD8(+) T lymphocytes, suggesting that MCAM could represent a biomarker of MS disease activity and a valid target for the treatment of neuroinflammatory conditions.
25869475.summary: In mice with EAE, blocking or depleting the MCAM protein on immune T cells reduced long-term nerve-related disability and limited their entry into the brain.

25896970.mechanism: Neutralizes IL-6, limiting microglia activation and inflammation
25896970.conclusion_quote: These data demonstrate that astrocyte-derived IL-6 is a key mediator of progressive disease and support IL-6 blockade as a viable intervention strategy to combat progressive MS.
25896970.summary: In mice with progressive EAE, blocking the inflammatory protein IL-6 after symptoms began reduced disability, myelin loss, and nerve damage.

26191196.mechanism: protects activated T cells from activation-induced death
26191196.conclusion_quote: Conclusions high dose of α-GC could be used as an adjuvant for inhibiting activation-induced CD4+ T and CD8+ T cell death.
26191196.summary: In mice with EAE, T cells treated with high-dose α-galactosylceramide caused more frequent and more severe disease, while tumor-targeting T cells survived longer.

25258010.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these findings have implications for the design and interpretation of microglia transcriptome-based investigations.
25258010.summary: In mice with EAE, microglia showed more oligodendrocyte and neuron gene transcripts, and how microglia were isolated changed which genes were detected.

26367776.mechanism: Not applicable, observational human gut microbiota study
26367776.conclusion_quote: Correcting the dysbiosis and altered gut microbiota might deserve consideration as a potential strategy for the prevention and treatment of MS.
26367776.summary: In a study of 20 Japanese patients with relapsing MS, gut bacteria differed from healthy people, with many clostridial species reduced. No animals or cells were used.

26163590.mechanism: Deletes IRF8 in T cells or retinal cells
26163590.conclusion_quote: These results raise a cautionary note in the context of therapeutic targeting of IRF8.
26163590.summary: In mice, removing IRF8 from T cells worsened eye inflammation, while removing it from retinal cells protected against experimental autoimmune uveitis, an eye disease rather than MS.

26714420.mechanism: Reduces IL-17 and IL-23 cytokine expression
26714420.conclusion_quote: Ginger extract reduces the expression of IL-17 and IL-23 in EAE mice.
26714420.summary: In mice with EAE, ginger extract given from early on lowered IL-17 and IL-23 levels in the spinal cord and blood.

26469270.mechanism: Lost receptor reduces microglial uptake of aggregated protein
26469270.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that one mechanism by which CX3CR1-/- attenuates inflammation is at the level of phagocytosis of aggregated α-syn by microglia.
26469270.summary: In mice modeling Parkinson disease, removing the CX3CR1 receptor reduced inflammation and microglial uptake of alpha-synuclein but did not worsen dopamine neuron loss.

25864579.mechanism: Modulates S1P receptors in atrioventricular node tissue
25864579.conclusion_quote: To our knowledge, these remarkable findings have not been previously reported in the literature, and stress the importance for extensive monitoring period in certain cases, especially in patients taking concurrently AV node blocker agents.
25864579.summary: In isolated rat heart tissue, the MS drug FTY720 slowed electrical conduction through the AV node and reduced ischaemia-related rhythm disturbances, with no disease model tested.

25819540.mechanism: Tissue digestion and cell separation method, not a treatment
25819540.conclusion_quote: We strongly believe that the field of neurosciences will benefit from an optimal use of flow cytometry to elucidate physiological and pathological processes.
25819540.summary: A new method for preparing mouse brain and spinal cord tissue lets researchers count neural and immune cells together by flow cytometry, tested in healthy and EAE mice.

25168393.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that a higher sodium intake is associated with increased clinical and radiological disease activity in patients with MS.
25168393.summary: In a human cohort of people with MS, higher urinary sodium, a sign of salt intake, was linked to more relapses and new brain lesions on MRI.

25617499.mechanism: Autoantigen to liver endothelium induces regulatory T cells
25617499.conclusion_quote: Our findings provide proof of principle that the selective delivery of autoantigen peptides to LSECs by NPs can induce antigen-specific Tregs and enable effective treatment of autoimmune disease.
25617499.summary: In mice with EAE, nanoparticles delivering autoantigen peptides to liver cells prevented disease and quickly improved established symptoms by boosting regulatory T cells.

26584020.mechanism: not tested, safety assessment only in healthy animals
26584020.conclusion_quote: Our results suggest that β-D-mannuronic acid is relatively safe when administered orally in animals.
26584020.summary: In healthy mice and rats, an anti-inflammatory drug called M2000 was tested for safety and was found relatively safe when given by mouth, with no MS model used.

25824601.mechanism: Induces suppressor T cells through skin immunization
25824601.conclusion_quote: The suppression of inflammatory responses by T suppressor cells induced through EC immunization of a protein antigen may become an attractive noninvasive therapeutic method for a variety of clinical situations.
25824601.summary: In mice with collagen-induced arthritis, a skin patch with collagen induced suppressor T cells that reduced joint inflammation and disease severity.

26438525.mechanism: not applicable, genetic variants in a diabetes model
26438525.conclusion_quote: In summary, we describe two new T1D loci, Idd18.2 and Idd18.4, candidate genes within each region, and demonstrate the complex nature of genetic interactions underlying the development of T1D in the NOD mouse model.
26438525.summary: In NOD mice, a model of type 1 diabetes, researchers identified two new genetic regions linked to the disease, pointing to candidate genes Ptpn22 and Cd2.

25938431.mechanism: Suppresses cytokine production and boosts regulatory T cells
25938431.conclusion_quote: Our study shows, for the first time, that violacein is able to modulate acute and chronic inflammation.
25938431.summary: In mice with EAE, the bacterial compound violacein given at disease onset produced milder symptoms and increased protective regulatory T cells.

26377397.conclusion_quote: Immunization of marmoset monkeys with rhMOG in IFA elicits clinical EAE in all animals.
26377397.summary: Marmoset monkeys immunized with human MOG protein in incomplete Freund's adjuvant all developed clinical EAE, showing that the adjuvant shapes which MOG regions trigger immune attacks.

26318182.conclusion_quote: Treg/Th17 cell imbalance in the optic nerve precedes and may initiate neuronal damage of axons and RGCs.
26318182.summary: In mice with experimental optic neuritis, an imbalance between immune cells called Treg and Th17 appeared before nerve and retinal cell damage, tracking vision loss.

26637322.conclusion_quote: In the present study, we established a severe experimental NMO rat model with highly clinical exacerbation and extensive tissue destructive lesions typically observed in NMO patients, which has not adequately been realized in in-vivo rodent models.
26637322.summary: In rats with EAE, injecting pathogenic anti-AQP4 antibodies produced severe NMO-like spinal cord and optic lesions, with the highest dose causing rapid worsening of symptoms.

26676788.summary: In mice infected with mouse hepatitis virus, a model of demyelination, astrocyte connexin43 levels fell and its ability to form working channels between cells was disrupted.

26559484.conclusion_quote: The results demonstrate the potential for CNS tissue destruction to induce and recruit SR T cells to the injury site and support a host suppressive mechanism limiting development of autoimmunity.
26559484.summary: In mice infected with a neurotropic coronavirus, researchers studied how immune cells that attack myelin are activated and fade after damage, finding they decline without causing lasting autoimmune disease.

25880134.mechanism: Induces EGR2-dependent T-cell anergy and shifts STAT3/STAT5 balance
25880134.conclusion_quote: Our data suggests that CBD exerts its immunoregulatory effects via induction of CD4(+)CD25(-)CD69(+)LAG3(+) cells in MOG35-55-activated APC/TMOG co-cultures.
25880134.summary: In mouse EAE immune cell cultures, cannabidiol made T cells less active and inflammatory, reducing their production of Th17 signals linked to disease.

25269572.mechanism: Enhances osmotic tolerance and suppresses acrosome reaction
25269572.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, the presence of trehalose in anisosmotic conditions enhances the osmotic tolerance, cryosurvival rate of ram spermatozoon and suppresses their ability to undergo LPC and cryo-induced acrosome reaction.
25269572.summary: Trehalose sugar helped ram sperm cells survive osmotic and freezing stress and reduced their premature acrosome reaction. This study does not involve multiple sclerosis.

25896927.mechanism: Describes IL-16 role in T cell inflammation
25896927.conclusion_quote: A cytokine IL-16 emerges as an important regulator of relapsing MS and EAE.
25896927.summary: In mice with relapsing EAE and in human MS brain tissue, researchers found that the immune protein IL-16 is linked to inflammation and nerve damage, without testing any treatment.

26023184.mechanism: Activates LXR nuclear receptors, boosting myelin gene expression and oligodendro
26023184.conclusion_quote: Together, our findings represent a conceptual advance in the transcriptional control of myelin gene expression and strongly support a new role of LXRs as positive modulators in central (re)myelination processes.
26023184.summary: In mice lacking LXR receptors and in cerebellar slice cultures, activating LXRs with drugs boosted myelin production and repaired myelin after chemical demyelination.

25774663.mechanism: Removes JunB and c-Jun from mature oligodendrocytes
25774663.conclusion_quote: We conclude that JunB and c-Jun expression in post-mitotic oligodendrocytes is mostly dispensable for the maintainance of white matter tracts throughout adult life, even under demyelinating conditions.
25774663.summary: In mice, deleting JunB and c-Jun from adult myelin-making cells did not kill them or cause clear demyelination, even when cuprizone was used to damage myelin.

25694088.conclusion_quote: The presented data support the idea that granules might be the result of an imbalance of redox-active metals and/or a dysregulation of complementary mechanisms that regulate their homeostasis in astrocyte-neuron coupling, respectively.
25694088.summary: In aging SJL/J mice, hippocampal granules formed over time and decreased after cuprizone, a copper chelator, but the study focuses on the granules rather than MS itself.

25631124.mechanism: Removing TREM2 reduces microglia activation and myelin debris clearance
25631124.conclusion_quote: These findings place TREM2 as a key regulator of microglia activation in vivo in response to tissue damage.
25631124.summary: In mice fed cuprizone to strip myelin, removing the TREM2 gene weakened microglia activation, slowed debris clearance, and increased nerve damage.

26142314.mechanism: Not applicable, no treatment or gene change tested
26142314.conclusion_quote: Altogether our results highlight a region and context-dependent contribution of SVZdNP to myelin repair that can equal pOPC.
26142314.summary: In mice fed cuprizone to damage myelin, brain stem cells near the ventricles helped repair myelin in some regions but barely contributed during long-lasting damage.

26370458.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, the embryo activation methods and sperm pretreatments examined in the present study did not affect the normal fertilization rate of bovine ICSI embryos.
26370458.summary: This study of cow embryos made by sperm injection tested activation methods and sperm treatments and found no change in fertilization. It does not involve multiple sclerosis.

26709696.mechanism: Prox1 loss boosts progenitor proliferation, reduces oligodendrocyte differentiat
26709696.conclusion_quote: Altogether, these data show that Prox1 is required to inhibit OPC proliferation and for OL differentiation, and could be a relevant component of the regenerative glial response.
26709696.summary: In mice, deleting the Prox1 gene from oligodendrocyte cells increased progenitor cell numbers, reduced mature oligodendrocytes, and weakened repair after lysolecithin-induced demyelination.

25948275.mechanism: Describes demyelination effects, no treatment tested
25948275.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that oligodendroglial myelination is not only important for maximizing conduction velocity, but also for limiting hyperexcitability of pyramidal neurons.
25948275.summary: In mice fed the cuprizone diet, demyelinated nerve fibers made neurons more excitable and moved the firing start point closer to the cell body.

25609628.mechanism: Activates monocytes and microglia via MyD88/TRIF signaling
25609628.conclusion_quote: Our results have identified candidates among currently used medications as potential therapies for the repair of myelin.
25609628.summary: In mice with spinal cord demyelination caused by lysolecithin, amphotericin B and MCSF activated immune cells and, especially together, increased myelin repair.

25852473.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes synaptic changes after demyelination
25852473.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our results demonstrate that newly-generated OPCs do not receive synaptic inputs during their active proliferation after demyelination, but gain synapses during the remyelination process.
25852473.summary: In mice with lysolecithin demyelination, newly made precursor cells lack synaptic input while proliferating, then regain synapses during remyelination.

25736969.mechanism: Lipid triggers calcium release from stores and influx
25736969.conclusion_quote: The LPC-induced [Ca(2+)]i increase in S2 cells was dependent on both the release of Ca(2+) stored in the endoplasmic reticulum and [Ca(2+)]e influx.
25736969.summary: In Drosophila S2 cells, lysophosphatidylcholine raised calcium levels mainly by releasing stored calcium and by letting in outside calcium.

26464826.mechanism: promotes progenitor recruitment and myelin repair
26464826.conclusion_quote: FGF2 enhanced hippocampal myelination and potentiated the recruitment of OPCs and neural stem cells (NSCs) to the lesion area.
26464826.summary: In rats with chemically induced hippocampal demyelination, FGF2 injections boosted myelin protein levels and attracted more myelin-forming and stem cells to the damaged area.

26330688.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, multiple lipids were associated with disease progression and provide clues regarding lipid drivers of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
26330688.summary: This study followed liver fat changes in mice fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet to model fatty liver disease, finding several lipids linked to worsening disease over time.

26132590.conclusion_quote: Overall, the present data suggest that the dietary fat source influenced performance, AMEN and fat retention in broiler chickens.
26132590.summary: In broiler chickens fed soy oil or tallow diets, higher phytase doses and an emulsifier changed growth and nutrient retention, but the study does not involve multiple sclerosis.
